# AI migrations: corrections, every lesson, every case line, the checklist and its guide, its report formats and the pitfalls in one file

Unofficial; company names describe the subject only. Summaries and lessons are our own words under CC BY 4.0. Source: https://github.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations

Disclosure: the cases and lessons are drafted by Claude, an Anthropic model, and reviewed by the maintainer. At least 16 of the 24 cases used Claude models or Claude Code (Bloomberg, Ping.gg, GitHub, Checkly, Intel, Bun, GitLab, Mindstone, Datadog, Lutz Leonhardt, PagerDuty, Ladybird, Christopher Chedeau, Spotify, Robert Marshall, Slack; 6 others leave the models unstated), and Anthropic owns Bun, the subject of one case. GitHub, Intel, Mindstone and Ping.gg also used other vendors' models; where a source compares outcomes by model, that is its author's own unaudited report, and no lesson ranks vendors.

The checklist and the lessons guide an agent through what the cases show; they do not decide for a project. Each question's guide gives the lessons in our words with links, what it looks like in a project, questions to ask, the trade-offs and when not to apply it; "ours" marks the maintainer's reading. A review reports findings and options with their trade-offs, and the project's owner chooses: do, later or skip.

## Corrections

What this collection published wrong, and how a project that applied it can find and repair it.
Every revisit reads this file first, before anything else, even while it has no entry: README step
1 of both routes when the project has a record, step 10 of the [checklist](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/checklist.md) and step 7
of [applying the lessons](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/docs/applying-lessons.md).

### How a revisit uses it

1. For each entry, compare its "Published" span with the project's record: the collection's commit
   or date and the log entry it names, and earlier versions of the record in the project's git
   history, if it is kept there. Compare by date: a commit counts by its date, a log entry by its
   heading's. The entry applies when any of them falls in the span.
2. For an entry that applies, look for it in the project as "How to recognise it" says, then follow
   "How to find what it changed": the record first, then the git history of the files that the
   record's applied items touched.
3. Report what you found for each entry, and turn its "What to propose" into options for the
   project's owner, each with its trade-off. Change nothing until the owner chooses (P1), except
   the record's "Corrections checked:" line (step 4).
4. In the record, write the entries you checked on its "Corrections checked:" line, with the date
   and what you found ("COR-1: not found", "COR-2: found, proposal 4"); with no entry, "none listed".
5. No entry, or none that applies: say so in one line and go on with the revisit.

While an entry exists, the README and [llms.txt](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/llms.txt) ask anyone who ran the checklist or the
lessons route during its span to run the revisit again.

### Entries

None yet.

### Provenance

Levels as in the [checklist](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/checklist.md#provenance).

| ID | Source | Level | Prevents | Blind failure |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| P1 | ours | ours | a repair the owner did not choose, made by an agent that trusts an entry over the project's own reasons | leaving a wrong rule at work in the project while the question waits; ask the owner at once |

Evidence base: every lesson here comes from the **migrations** in this collection, all done with AI except one rule-based contrast case; many apply to large engineering work done with AI agents generally.

`[stated]`: a source says it or reports it as what worked or failed. `[ours]`: our inference from what a source reports. "Old system as oracle" (`yes`, `partly`, `no`): does the evidence rely on the old system (its tests, its outputs, its users' reports) to tell right from wrong; it says where the evidence came from, not where the lesson applies. "Depends on model ability" (`yes`, `partly`, `no`): `yes` when the lesson states what models or agents can or cannot do, `partly` when it is a process whose need comes from such a behaviour, `no` when it holds whatever the model; the index marks a `yes` lesson whose newest case is over a year old as possibly outdated. "Era": the years the cited cases ran (their publication year when they give no period), then the newest model family: the family of the most recent cited case that names a model (its highest version when it names several), `unstated` when none names one; each case lists all its models. "Strength", capped by the cases in "Cases" (the validator checks it): `strong` needs two or more cases, or one whose source shows its data, and at least one case whose author does not sell the tool; `medium` needs two or more cases, or one that shows its data; any other lesson is `weak`. So a seller's case weighs less: a lesson that rests only on such cases is at most `medium`.

## Planning and scoping (planning.md)

How to size, slice, order and stage a large piece of AI-driven work before agents touch the code.

- **PLN-1** [stated] Pilot the whole pipeline (build, CI, review, packaging, release) on a few easy, well-tested units, and settle the conventions before fanning out to the rest.
  - Old system as oracle: partly. Depends on model ability: no. Strength: strong. Era: 2024–2026; newest: Claude Opus 5.x.
  - Cases: [Bun: what worked](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2026-07-08-bun-zig-to-rust.md#what-worked), [GitHub: what worked](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2026-09-16-github-copilot-runtime-rust.md#what-worked), [Google: what worked](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2025-04-13-google-int64-ids.md#what-worked), [Airbnb: who did what](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2025-04-01-airbnb-enzyme-to-rtl.md#who-did-what), [Spartacus: what worked](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2026-04-13-lutz-leonhardt-spartacus-signal-forms.md#what-worked), [Spartacus: what went wrong](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2026-04-13-lutz-leonhardt-spartacus-signal-forms.md#what-went-wrong).
  - Against: Bun's three-file trial did not reveal the clash between agents sharing one checkout that hit minutes into the full run ([Bun](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2026-07-08-bun-zig-to-rust.md#what-went-wrong)).
- **PLN-2** [stated] Expect most of the effort to go into specs, porting guides, manifests and tooling before the bulk run; schedule and staff that phase, not only execution.
  - Old system as oracle: no. Depends on model ability: no. Strength: strong. Era: 2025–2026; newest: Claude Opus 5.x.
  - Cases: [1Password: what worked](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2026-04-20-1password-monolith-refactor.md#what-worked), [Bun: what worked](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2026-07-08-bun-zig-to-rust.md#what-worked), [GitHub: what worked](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2026-09-16-github-copilot-runtime-rust.md#what-worked), [Uber: what worked](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2026-04-07-uber-junit4-to-junit5.md#what-worked).
  - Against: At Airbnb the bulk run was quick, but the long tail then took days of tuning and a week by hand ([Airbnb](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2025-04-01-airbnb-enzyme-to-rtl.md#what-went-wrong)): the tail is the other large cost.
- **PLN-3** [stated] Re-measure scope while the work runs; in a live repository, code moving into scope and code written meanwhile can multiply the first estimate.
  - Old system as oracle: no. Depends on model ability: no. Strength: medium. Era: 2026; newest: Claude Opus 5.x.
  - Cases: [GitHub: what went wrong](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2026-09-16-github-copilot-runtime-rust.md#what-went-wrong).
  - Against: None found; the Airbnb file set was fixed, so it had no inflow ([Airbnb](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2025-04-01-airbnb-enzyme-to-rtl.md#numbers)).
- **PLN-4** [stated] Order the slices along the dependency graph, leaves first and the most connected hub last, and approach the hub from one direction only.
  - Old system as oracle: no. Depends on model ability: no. Strength: medium. Era: 2026; newest: Claude Opus 5.x.
  - Cases: [GitHub: what worked](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2026-09-16-github-copilot-runtime-rust.md#what-worked), [GitHub: what went wrong](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2026-09-16-github-copilot-runtime-rust.md#what-went-wrong), [Intel: who did what](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2026-08-24-intel-ideas-c-to-rust.md#who-did-what), [1Password: what worked](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2026-04-20-1password-monolith-refactor.md#what-worked).
  - Against: Disagree: the Pokémon Showdown port went through methods in list order with no working slices and joined them only at the end, then fixed what diverged from the old engine ([Pokémon](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2026-01-25-vjeux-pokemon-showdown-rust.md#what-worked)); our reading is that a full old-engine oracle made the order matter less.
- **PLN-5** [stated] Translate first and redesign later: keep behaviour the same during the move so that any failure points at the port, not at a deliberate change.
  - Old system as oracle: yes. Depends on model ability: no. Strength: medium. Era: 2025–2026; newest: GPT-6.x.
  - Cases: [GitHub: practices to copy](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2026-09-16-github-copilot-runtime-rust.md#practices-to-copy), [Bun: what worked](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2026-07-08-bun-zig-to-rust.md#what-worked), [Pokémon: what was migrated](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2026-01-25-vjeux-pokemon-showdown-rust.md#what-was-migrated), [ts-rust: what was migrated](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2026-10-07-ping-tsgo-to-rust.md#what-was-migrated), [Ladybird: what went wrong](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2026-02-23-ladybird-libjs-rust.md#what-went-wrong), [Mindstone: what was migrated](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2026-07-06-mindstone-go-to-typescript.md#what-was-migrated), [Checkly: what went wrong](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2026-09-01-checkly-nodejs-to-go.md#what-went-wrong).
  - Against: Disagree: Intel aims for idiomatic data structures at translation time ([Intel](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2026-08-24-intel-ideas-c-to-rust.md#practices-to-copy)), and GitHub's own review prompt asked for idiomatic, optimised code during the port. Shopify retired or simplified some Shop screens during the move, though each checkpoint still had to match the running old app ([Shopify](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2026-09-10-shopify-react-native-to-native.md#what-was-migrated), [checkpoints](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2026-09-10-shopify-react-native-to-native.md#how-it-was-checked)). Datadog ruled out keeping its key-value model on the new database, whose heaviest operations were estimated far too slow, and people redesigned the schema before the port, while the old tests still judged behaviour ([Datadog](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2026-06-23-datadog-foundationdb-to-postgres.md#what-went-wrong), [checks](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2026-06-23-datadog-foundationdb-to-postgres.md#how-it-was-checked)). A Gatsby-to-Next.js move failed when the agent ported the old design faithfully, data layers included, and worked once the target's architecture was built first ([Gatsby blog](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2025-08-09-robert-marshall-gatsby-to-nextjs.md#what-went-wrong)).
- **PLN-6** [stated] Set expectations per class of work: bounded, repetitive edits gain a lot; work with ordering, schema or shared-state constraints gains far less.
  - Old system as oracle: no. Depends on model ability: yes. Strength: medium. Era: 2024–2026; newest: Claude (version unstated).
  - Cases: [1Password: what worked](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2026-04-20-1password-monolith-refactor.md#what-worked), [1Password: what went wrong](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2026-04-20-1password-monolith-refactor.md#what-went-wrong), [Spotify: numbers](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2025-11-06-spotify-honk.md#numbers), [Zalando: what went wrong](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2025-02-20-zalando-ui-component-libraries.md#what-went-wrong), [Temporal: what worked](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2026-09-02-temporal-billing-store-clickhouse.md#what-worked).
  - Against: Uber's repetitive test-framework move did not work with generative AI over several files at once, which the authors put down to scale and in-house test patterns ([Uber](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2026-04-07-uber-junit4-to-junit5.md#what-went-wrong)).
  - Related view (karpathy-ideas): [coding agents weak on novel code](https://github.com/ntroccoli/karpathy-ideas/blob/main/ideas/2025-10-17-coding-agents-weak-on-novel-code.md), agrees.
- **PLN-7** [ours] Reopen rewrites shelved for cost, since agents change the price; but weigh them against doing nothing, not against a manual rewrite nobody would fund.
  - Old system as oracle: no. Depends on model ability: partly. Strength: medium. Era: 2026; newest: Claude Opus 5.x.
  - Cases: [Bun: numbers](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2026-07-08-bun-zig-to-rust.md#numbers), [GitHub: context](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2026-09-16-github-copilot-runtime-rust.md#context), [1Password: what worked](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2026-04-20-1password-monolith-refactor.md#what-worked).
  - Against: Slack had no do-nothing option: the old library blocked a framework upgrade ([Slack](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2024-05-22-slack-enzyme-to-rtl.md#context)); service extraction at 1Password gained only modestly ([1Password](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2026-04-20-1password-monolith-refactor.md#what-went-wrong)); and at Temporal the teardown teams usually defer became cheap, but the authors credit habits already in place more than the model ([Temporal](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2026-09-02-temporal-billing-store-clickhouse.md#what-worked)).
- **PLN-8** [stated] Leave out segments you cannot specify or verify (non-standard repositories, unsupported platforms, languages the model handles poorly) instead of forcing one approach on all.
  - Old system as oracle: no. Depends on model ability: partly. Strength: medium. Era: 2025–2026; newest: Claude Opus 4.x.
  - Cases: [Spotify: what went wrong](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2025-11-06-spotify-honk.md#what-went-wrong), [Google: what went wrong](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2025-04-13-google-int64-ids.md#what-went-wrong), [Uber: what worked](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2026-04-07-uber-junit4-to-junit5.md#what-worked), [Bloomberg: what worked](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2026-11-03-bloomberg-python-cpp-uplift.md#what-worked).
  - Against: Bloomberg did not leave its rare archetypes out: each got a generic starting-point PR, labelled as such, for its owners to finish ([Bloomberg](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2026-11-03-bloomberg-python-cpp-uplift.md#what-went-wrong)).
- **PLN-9** [ours] Plan for a partial outcome and a stop rule: abandoned attempts appear here only inside stories that end in a success, so success odds read from such cases are inflated.
  - Old system as oracle: no. Depends on model ability: no. Strength: medium. Era: 2024–2026; newest: GPT-6.x.
  - Cases: [Slack: what went wrong](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2024-05-22-slack-enzyme-to-rtl.md#what-went-wrong), [1Password: what went wrong](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2026-04-20-1password-monolith-refactor.md#what-went-wrong), [Spotify: what went wrong](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2025-11-06-spotify-honk.md#what-went-wrong), [Airbnb: what went wrong](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2025-04-01-airbnb-enzyme-to-rtl.md#what-went-wrong), [ts-rust: what went wrong](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2026-10-07-ping-tsgo-to-rust.md#what-went-wrong), [Gatsby blog: what went wrong](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2025-08-09-robert-marshall-gatsby-to-nextjs.md#what-went-wrong).
  - Against: Uber reports an AI attempt that failed and was dropped, a first in this collection, though it names no model, size or date ([Uber](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2026-04-07-uber-junit4-to-junit5.md#what-went-wrong)); ts-rust reports a first attempt that ran for months below its target before a restart replaced its code, with no stop rule stated ([ts-rust](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2026-10-07-ping-tsgo-to-rust.md#what-went-wrong)); the migrations themselves are all survivors.
- **PLN-10** [stated] Measure how often each pattern (runner, rule, base class) is used and how automatable it is, and build the transforms or prompts with the best return first.
  - Old system as oracle: no. Depends on model ability: partly. Strength: medium. Era: 2025–2026; newest: Claude Opus 4.x.
  - Cases: [Uber: what worked](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2026-04-07-uber-junit4-to-junit5.md#what-worked), [Bloomberg: what worked](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2026-11-03-bloomberg-python-cpp-uplift.md#what-worked).
  - Against: None found; Bloomberg's authors say easier archetypes may have gone first, which can inflate early success rates ([Bloomberg](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2026-11-03-bloomberg-python-cpp-uplift.md#what-went-wrong)).
- **PLN-11** [stated] Do not port a whole app in one pass, even from specs gathered first; Shopify's author says that gives code nobody can maintain. Port in small ordered slices a person can review quickly.
  - Old system as oracle: partly. Depends on model ability: partly. Strength: weak. Era: 2025–2026; newest: unstated.
  - Cases: [Shopify: what went wrong](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2026-09-10-shopify-react-native-to-native.md#what-went-wrong), [Shopify: how it was checked](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2026-09-10-shopify-react-native-to-native.md#how-it-was-checked), [Pokémon: what went wrong](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2026-01-25-vjeux-pokemon-showdown-rust.md#what-went-wrong).
  - Against: Disagree: Bun merged a whole port as one branch ([Bun](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2026-07-08-bun-zig-to-rust.md#what-worked)), though built from many agent-sized units, not in one pass. Ladybird likewise steered its port in many small prompts but merged it as one large pull request a day after opening it ([Ladybird](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2026-02-23-ladybird-libjs-rust.md#who-did-what)). After its failed one-shot attempt (cited above), the same Pokémon Showdown port ported every method before running any of it and joined them once, arguing that growing it slice by slice would relearn settled design ([Pokémon](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2026-01-25-vjeux-pokemon-showdown-rust.md#what-worked)).
- **PLN-12** [stated] Sort targets into archetypes, each with its own prompt, data collection and checks; give rare archetypes a generic starting point instead of dedicated automation.
  - Old system as oracle: no. Depends on model ability: partly. Strength: medium. Era: 2025–2026; newest: Claude Opus 4.x.
  - Cases: [Bloomberg: what worked](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2026-11-03-bloomberg-python-cpp-uplift.md#what-worked), [Bloomberg: what went wrong](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2026-11-03-bloomberg-python-cpp-uplift.md#what-went-wrong), [Mindstone: what worked](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2026-07-06-mindstone-go-to-typescript.md#what-worked), [Mindstone: what went wrong](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2026-07-06-mindstone-go-to-typescript.md#what-went-wrong).
  - Against: Airbnb ran one pipeline over all its files and grouped the failures by status afterwards; its case reports no sorting up front ([Airbnb](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2025-04-01-airbnb-enzyme-to-rtl.md#what-worked)).
- **PLN-13** [stated] In a framework or data-store move, build the target's foundation (architecture, data model) in its own idiom first, then port old parts onto it; one straight port rebuilt the old layers.
  - Old system as oracle: no. Depends on model ability: partly. Strength: weak. Era: 2025–2026; newest: Claude (version unstated).
  - Cases: [Gatsby blog: what went wrong](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2025-08-09-robert-marshall-gatsby-to-nextjs.md#what-went-wrong), [Gatsby blog: what worked](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2025-08-09-robert-marshall-gatsby-to-nextjs.md#what-worked), [Datadog: who did what](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2026-06-23-datadog-foundationdb-to-postgres.md#who-did-what), [Datadog: what went wrong](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2026-06-23-datadog-foundationdb-to-postgres.md#what-went-wrong).
  - Against: None found; language ports judged against the old system did the opposite, translating the old design first ([Ladybird](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2026-02-23-ladybird-libjs-rust.md#what-went-wrong), [Mindstone](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2026-07-06-mindstone-go-to-typescript.md#what-was-migrated)), and Gatsby is one small blog, and Datadog ruled out its straight port on an estimate without building it ([Datadog](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2026-06-23-datadog-foundationdb-to-postgres.md#what-went-wrong)).

## Testing and oracles (testing.md)

What tells you the new code is right, and where those oracles fail.

- **TST-1** [stated] Use a black-box suite that does not depend on the implementation language as the oracle: fix it before the port, review every edit to it, and run it against the old code and the new.
  - Old system as oracle: yes. Depends on model ability: no. Strength: strong. Era: 2025–2026; newest: GPT-6.x.
  - Cases: [Bun: how it was checked](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2026-07-08-bun-zig-to-rust.md#how-it-was-checked), [GitHub: how it was checked](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2026-09-16-github-copilot-runtime-rust.md#how-it-was-checked), [ts-rust: how it was checked](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2026-10-07-ping-tsgo-to-rust.md#how-it-was-checked), [Ladybird: how it was checked](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2026-02-23-ladybird-libjs-rust.md#how-it-was-checked), [Datadog: how it was checked](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2026-06-23-datadog-foundationdb-to-postgres.md#how-it-was-checked), [Mindstone: how it was checked](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2026-07-06-mindstone-go-to-typescript.md#how-it-was-checked), [Checkly: how it was checked](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2026-09-01-checkly-nodejs-to-go.md#how-it-was-checked).
  - Against: An outside critic asks why a suite that let the old bugs through should vet the new code ([Bun](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2026-07-08-bun-zig-to-rust.md#what-went-wrong)); Bun still shipped known regressions after a fully green run. The suite itself often moved: Ladybird's pull request edited 42 expected-output files of its own tests while test262 stayed unchanged ([Ladybird](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2026-02-23-ladybird-libjs-rust.md#what-went-wrong)); Checkly changed its harness during the move and still missed production's queue layout ([Checkly](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2026-09-01-checkly-nodejs-to-go.md#what-went-wrong)); Mindstone's suite was written by agents during the move, and its first version asserted nothing ([Mindstone](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2026-07-06-mindstone-go-to-typescript.md#what-went-wrong)); Datadog's tests checked only fixtures, so it added weeks of live comparison ([Datadog](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2026-06-23-datadog-foundationdb-to-postgres.md#how-it-was-checked)).
  - Related view (karpathy-ideas): [port with equality tests](https://github.com/ntroccoli/karpathy-ideas/blob/main/ideas/2026-01-03-port-with-equality-tests.md), agrees.
- **TST-2** [stated] Before the move starts, make sure tests cover the behaviour that matters and that agents can run them; the gaps were where missing-feature regressions came from.
  - Old system as oracle: yes. Depends on model ability: no. Strength: medium. Era: 2025–2026; newest: GPT-6.x.
  - Cases: [GitHub: what went wrong](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2026-09-16-github-copilot-runtime-rust.md#what-went-wrong), [Spotify: practices to copy](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2025-11-06-spotify-honk.md#practices-to-copy), [ts-rust: what went wrong](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2026-10-07-ping-tsgo-to-rust.md#what-went-wrong), [Spartacus: what went wrong](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2026-04-13-lutz-leonhardt-spartacus-signal-forms.md#what-went-wrong), [Checkly: what went wrong](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2026-09-01-checkly-nodejs-to-go.md#what-went-wrong).
  - Against: Google leaned on the owning teams' existing regression suites and slow rollouts rather than new tests ([Google](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2025-04-13-google-int64-ids.md#how-it-was-checked)); Intel left the tests out on purpose and got a build that crashed ([Intel](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2026-08-24-intel-ideas-c-to-rust.md#what-went-wrong)).
- **TST-3** [stated] Equivalence with the old system is not correctness: a faithful port carries the old bugs, and tests can assert the wrong behaviour with confidence.
  - Old system as oracle: yes. Depends on model ability: no. Strength: medium. Era: 2026; newest: Claude Opus 5.x.
  - Cases: [Bun: what went wrong](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2026-07-08-bun-zig-to-rust.md#what-went-wrong), [GitHub: what went wrong](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2026-09-16-github-copilot-runtime-rust.md#what-went-wrong).
  - Against: The Bun rewrite also fixed many bugs that the old code had ([Bun](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2026-07-08-bun-zig-to-rust.md#what-went-wrong)), so a port is not only a copy of old defects.
  - Related view (karpathy-ideas): [port with equality tests](https://github.com/ntroccoli/karpathy-ideas/blob/main/ideas/2026-01-03-port-with-equality-tests.md), contradicts: equality with the reference also carries the reference's bugs and its wrong tests into the port.
- **TST-4** [ours] Run the oracle on the build configuration you ship; debug-only assertions and checks hid regressions that appeared only in release builds.
  - Old system as oracle: partly. Depends on model ability: no. Strength: weak. Era: 2026; newest: Claude Fable 5.x.
  - Cases: [Bun: what went wrong](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2026-07-08-bun-zig-to-rust.md#what-went-wrong).
  - Against: None found.
- **TST-5** [stated] Where the old system has thin tests, record its inputs and outputs (or have a separate agent write equivalence tests) and replay them against the new code.
  - Old system as oracle: yes. Depends on model ability: partly. Strength: medium. Era: 2024–2026; newest: Claude Fable (version unstated).
  - Cases: [Intel: what worked](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2026-08-24-intel-ideas-c-to-rust.md#what-worked), [Slack: what worked](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2024-05-22-slack-enzyme-to-rtl.md#what-worked), [Mindstone: who did what](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2026-07-06-mindstone-go-to-typescript.md#who-did-what), [Checkly: how it was checked](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2026-09-01-checkly-nodejs-to-go.md#how-it-was-checked).
  - Against: Full coverage through a library's public functions is often out of reach, and generated tests can be vacuous ([Intel](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2026-08-24-intel-ideas-c-to-rust.md#what-went-wrong)); Mindstone's first agent-written suite asserted nothing and was regenerated under stricter rules ([Mindstone](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2026-07-06-mindstone-go-to-typescript.md#what-went-wrong)). The Pokémon port ran both versions live on seeded inputs rather than recording, and does not say the old tests were thin ([Pokémon](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2026-01-25-vjeux-pokemon-showdown-rust.md#how-it-was-checked)).
- **TST-6** [stated] Make the baseline green before agents start: fix tests that already fail and make golden files regenerable, or correct changes stall at the gate.
  - Old system as oracle: yes. Depends on model ability: no. Strength: medium. Era: 2025–2026; newest: Claude (version unstated).
  - Cases: [Google: what went wrong](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2025-04-13-google-int64-ids.md#what-went-wrong), [Spotify: how it was checked](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2025-11-06-spotify-honk.md#how-it-was-checked).
  - Against: Spartacus's refined protocol lets an agent go on from a red baseline, noted as an old failure, and stops only when the tests will not start ([Spartacus](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2026-04-13-lutz-leonhardt-spartacus-signal-forms.md#how-it-was-checked)).
- **TST-7** [ours] When a move touches numeric types or sums (a widened ID, a new engine's arithmetic), test values beyond the old range at real data sizes; small examples pass while overflow survives.
  - Old system as oracle: partly. Depends on model ability: no. Strength: medium. Era: 2025–2026; newest: Gemini (internal).
  - Cases: [Google: what was migrated](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2025-04-13-google-int64-ids.md#what-was-migrated), [Temporal: what went wrong](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2026-09-02-temporal-billing-store-clickhouse.md#what-went-wrong).
  - Against: None found.
- **TST-8** [ours] When the migrated artefact is itself a test, passing is a weak oracle; also compare test counts, coverage and intent file by file.
  - Old system as oracle: yes. Depends on model ability: no. Strength: weak. Era: 2024–2026; newest: Claude 2.x.
  - Cases: [Slack: practices to copy](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2024-05-22-slack-enzyme-to-rtl.md#practices-to-copy), [Airbnb: how it was checked](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2025-04-01-airbnb-enzyme-to-rtl.md#how-it-was-checked), [Uber: how it was checked](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2026-04-07-uber-junit4-to-junit5.md#how-it-was-checked), [Asana: how it was checked](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2026-08-07-asana-enzyme-to-rtl.md#how-it-was-checked).
  - Against: None found; Airbnb says coverage and intent were kept, and Asana that coverage rose, but neither shows a method or figures.
- **TST-9** [stated] Treat performance as part of the contract: benchmark end to end against a deterministic local stand-in for slow services, and count slowdowns as regressions.
  - Old system as oracle: yes. Depends on model ability: no. Strength: medium. Era: 2026; newest: Claude Opus 5.x.
  - Cases: [GitHub: what went wrong](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2026-09-16-github-copilot-runtime-rust.md#what-went-wrong), [GitHub: numbers](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2026-09-16-github-copilot-runtime-rust.md#numbers), [Ladybird: how it was checked](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2026-02-23-ladybird-libjs-rust.md#how-it-was-checked).
  - Against: GitHub's own before-and-after mixes in other changes from the same months, which the author flags.
- **TST-10** [ours] Keep the agent that writes code apart from the one that writes its tests; one generation producing both invites checks that cannot fail.
  - Old system as oracle: no. Depends on model ability: partly. Strength: weak. Era: 2026; newest: GPT-5.x.
  - Cases: [Intel: what went wrong](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2026-08-24-intel-ideas-c-to-rust.md#what-went-wrong), [Intel: practices to copy](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2026-08-24-intel-ideas-c-to-rust.md#practices-to-copy).
  - Against: When generated separately, Intel's agent-written tests worked as well as expert ones as feedback ([Intel](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2026-08-24-intel-ideas-c-to-rust.md#what-worked)).
- **TST-11** [stated] Test the prompts too: rerun a golden set of before-and-after examples after each prompt edit or model trial; small wording changes swung results.
  - Old system as oracle: no. Depends on model ability: partly. Strength: weak. Era: 2024–2025; newest: GPT-4o.
  - Cases: [Zalando: how it was checked](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2025-02-20-zalando-ui-component-libraries.md#how-it-was-checked), [Zalando: what went wrong](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2025-02-20-zalando-ui-component-libraries.md#what-went-wrong).
  - Against: None found.
- **TST-12** [stated] Check parity on what users and downstream systems see: capture screens, raw events or query answers from old and new at the same points, ignoring values that vary per run.
  - Old system as oracle: yes. Depends on model ability: no. Strength: medium. Era: 2024–2026; newest: Claude (version unstated).
  - Cases: [Shopify: how it was checked](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2026-09-10-shopify-react-native-to-native.md#how-it-was-checked), [Zalando: how it was checked](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2025-02-20-zalando-ui-component-libraries.md#how-it-was-checked), [Datadog: how it was checked](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2026-06-23-datadog-foundationdb-to-postgres.md#how-it-was-checked), [Temporal: how it was checked](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2026-09-02-temporal-billing-store-clickhouse.md#how-it-was-checked).
  - Against: None found; Zalando calls for visual testing without saying how it compared the two, and Shopify does not say how far parity reached beyond the flows engineers ran ([Shopify](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2026-09-10-shopify-react-native-to-native.md#what-went-wrong)).
- **TST-13** [stated] Make the old code's output deterministic and dumpable before porting, then run old and new side by side on real or seeded inputs and stop at the first difference.
  - Old system as oracle: yes. Depends on model ability: no. Strength: medium. Era: 2025–2026; newest: unstated.
  - Cases: [Ladybird: how it was checked](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2026-02-23-ladybird-libjs-rust.md#how-it-was-checked), [Ladybird: who did what](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2026-02-23-ladybird-libjs-rust.md#who-did-what), [Pokémon: how it was checked](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2026-01-25-vjeux-pokemon-showdown-rust.md#how-it-was-checked).
  - Against: Checkly and Mindstone masked values that vary per run (typed placeholders, audited wildcards) instead of making the old code deterministic ([Checkly](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2026-09-01-checkly-nodejs-to-go.md#how-it-was-checked), [Mindstone](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2026-07-06-mindstone-go-to-typescript.md#how-it-was-checked)); Ladybird does not say how long the side-by-side browsing ran or which sites it covered ([Ladybird](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2026-02-23-ladybird-libjs-rust.md#what-went-wrong)).
  - Related view (karpathy-ideas): [port with equality tests](https://github.com/ntroccoli/karpathy-ideas/blob/main/ideas/2026-01-03-port-with-equality-tests.md), agrees.
- **TST-14** [stated] Never make coverage alone the target of agent-written tests: it rose while the tests asserted nothing. Fail any test that leaves a side effect or response field unasserted.
  - Old system as oracle: no. Depends on model ability: partly. Strength: weak. Era: 2026; newest: OpenAI Codex 5.x.
  - Cases: [Mindstone: what went wrong](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2026-07-06-mindstone-go-to-typescript.md#what-went-wrong), [Mindstone: what worked](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2026-07-06-mindstone-go-to-typescript.md#what-worked).
  - Against: None found; Mindstone's final pipeline still opens with a coverage push, and it counts no hollow tests before or after the rule ([Mindstone](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2026-07-06-mindstone-go-to-typescript.md#who-did-what), [numbers](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2026-07-06-mindstone-go-to-typescript.md#numbers)).
- **TST-15** [stated] Model the harness's surrounding infrastructure on production down to each queue and table; the agent builds to what the tests show, so a simplified layout ships as a bug.
  - Old system as oracle: partly. Depends on model ability: partly. Strength: weak. Era: 2026; newest: Claude Fable (version unstated).
  - Cases: [Checkly: what went wrong](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2026-09-01-checkly-nodejs-to-go.md#what-went-wrong).
  - Against: None found; one case, whose harness recorded outputs from the old daemon yet missed what only production's queue routing showed.

## Verification loops and gates (verification.md)

The automated checks around each agent change, and what they can and cannot prove.

- **VER-1** [stated] A clean compile or a green CI run shows the parts fit together, not that behaviour survived; plan a behavioural check after it.
  - Old system as oracle: partly. Depends on model ability: no. Strength: strong. Era: 2024–2026; newest: Claude Opus 4.x.
  - Cases: [GitHub: what went wrong](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2026-09-16-github-copilot-runtime-rust.md#what-went-wrong), [Intel: what went wrong](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2026-08-24-intel-ideas-c-to-rust.md#what-went-wrong), [Spotify: what went wrong](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2025-11-06-spotify-honk.md#what-went-wrong), [Zalando: what went wrong](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2025-02-20-zalando-ui-component-libraries.md#what-went-wrong), [Bloomberg: what went wrong](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2026-11-03-bloomberg-python-cpp-uplift.md#what-went-wrong), [Pokémon: what went wrong](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2026-01-25-vjeux-pokemon-showdown-rust.md#what-went-wrong), [Spartacus: how it was checked](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2026-04-13-lutz-leonhardt-spartacus-signal-forms.md#how-it-was-checked), [PagerDuty: what went wrong](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2026-04-13-pagerduty-rundeck-grails-7.md#what-went-wrong).
  - Against: In a memory-safe target, one class of memory bugs does become a compile error ([Bun](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2026-07-08-bun-zig-to-rust.md#how-it-was-checked)), so the compiler is a real but narrow check; Bloomberg calls a clean compile a strong sign of a right change when only build files move, though it still ran the unit tests after the build ([Bloomberg](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2026-11-03-bloomberg-python-cpp-uplift.md#what-worked)).
- **VER-2** [stated] Order gates from cheap to costly and drop a candidate at its first failure, with cheap no-change checks (whitespace only, unchanged syntax tree) up front.
  - Old system as oracle: partly. Depends on model ability: no. Strength: medium. Era: 2025–2026; newest: Gemini (internal).
  - Cases: [Google: how it was checked](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2025-04-13-google-int64-ids.md#how-it-was-checked), [Uber: how it was checked](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2026-04-07-uber-junit4-to-junit5.md#how-it-was-checked).
  - Against: Airbnb ran the tests before lint and type checks and retried a failed step instead of dropping the file ([Airbnb](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2025-04-01-airbnb-enzyme-to-rtl.md#what-worked)); Slack and Spotify send failures back to the model ([Slack](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2024-05-22-slack-enzyme-to-rtl.md#what-worked), [Spotify](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2025-11-06-spotify-honk.md#how-it-was-checked)).
- **VER-3** [stated] Retry a failed unit with its latest errors in a fresh prompt, cap the attempts, and hand what remains to people; this fits independent units, such as one file each.
  - Old system as oracle: partly. Depends on model ability: partly. Strength: strong. Era: 2024–2026; newest: Claude Opus 4.x.
  - Cases: [Airbnb: what worked](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2025-04-01-airbnb-enzyme-to-rtl.md#what-worked), [Google: who did what](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2025-04-13-google-int64-ids.md#who-did-what), [Spotify: numbers](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2025-11-06-spotify-honk.md#numbers), [Bloomberg: who did what](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2026-11-03-bloomberg-python-cpp-uplift.md#who-did-what).
  - Against: Google's developers could not tell how many retries a file would need ([Google](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2025-04-13-google-int64-ids.md#what-went-wrong)); test feedback helped one model on Intel's battery far more than another ([Intel](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2026-08-24-intel-ideas-c-to-rust.md#what-worked)); Uber neither retried nor handed over files whose tests failed but put them back on the old framework, as diagnosing each was impractical ([Uber](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2026-04-07-uber-junit4-to-junit5.md#what-went-wrong)); in Bun's port, where units depended on each other, the engineer fixed the workflow prompt instead of handing units to people ([Bun](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2026-07-08-bun-zig-to-rust.md#practices-to-copy)).
- **VER-4** [stated] Give the agent one verify tool that picks the right build and test runner and returns short errors, and run it automatically before the agent may finish.
  - Old system as oracle: partly. Depends on model ability: partly. Strength: weak. Era: 2025–2026; newest: Claude (version unstated).
  - Cases: [Spotify: what worked](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2025-11-06-spotify-honk.md#what-worked), [Spotify: practices to copy](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2025-11-06-spotify-honk.md#practices-to-copy), [Datadog: what went wrong](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2026-06-23-datadog-foundationdb-to-postgres.md#what-went-wrong).
  - Against: GitHub's agents called the raw build and test commands directly, in large volume, and still finished ([GitHub](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2026-09-16-github-copilot-runtime-rust.md#numbers)).
- **VER-5** [stated] Before trusting a green suite, confirm the tests really ran: compare executed tests and assertions with the baseline, and count skips as failures.
  - Old system as oracle: yes. Depends on model ability: no. Strength: medium. Era: 2024–2026; newest: Claude Fable 5.x.
  - Cases: [Bun: how it was checked](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2026-07-08-bun-zig-to-rust.md#how-it-was-checked), [Bun: practices to copy](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2026-07-08-bun-zig-to-rust.md#practices-to-copy), [Slack: what went wrong](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2024-05-22-slack-enzyme-to-rtl.md#what-went-wrong), [Spartacus: what went wrong](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2026-04-13-lutz-leonhardt-spartacus-signal-forms.md#what-went-wrong).
  - Against: None found; in Spartacus's second run the tests did run and pass, and in our reading a changed email rule still got through ([Spartacus](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2026-04-13-lutz-leonhardt-spartacus-signal-forms.md#what-went-wrong)): a run check does not replace coverage.
- **VER-6** [stated] Check output against machine-readable contracts (generated signatures, schema-compatibility checks) so a dropped or changed interface fails mechanically.
  - Old system as oracle: partly. Depends on model ability: no. Strength: medium. Era: 2026; newest: Claude Opus 5.x.
  - Cases: [Intel: what worked](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2026-08-24-intel-ideas-c-to-rust.md#what-worked), [GitHub: what went wrong](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2026-09-16-github-copilot-runtime-rust.md#what-went-wrong).
  - Against: At GitHub the agent silenced the schema check with its waiver label and only human review caught it ([GitHub](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2026-09-16-github-copilot-runtime-rust.md#what-went-wrong)); a contract check needs its bypass behind approval.
- **VER-7** [stated] Define done as an empty list of change sites produced by deterministic tooling and rerun on a schedule, never as the agent's own report.
  - Old system as oracle: partly. Depends on model ability: partly. Strength: medium. Era: 2025–2026; newest: Claude (version unstated).
  - Cases: [Google: what worked](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2025-04-13-google-int64-ids.md#what-worked), [1Password: what worked](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2026-04-20-1password-monolith-refactor.md#what-worked), [Pokémon: what worked](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2026-01-25-vjeux-pokemon-showdown-rust.md#what-worked), [Spartacus: what went wrong](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2026-04-13-lutz-leonhardt-spartacus-signal-forms.md#what-went-wrong), [GitLab: what went wrong](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2026-07-08-gitlab-rate-limiting.md#what-went-wrong).
  - Against: Google's reference search stops after a set number of hops and can miss sites ([Google](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2025-04-13-google-int64-ids.md#what-went-wrong)); the Pokémon port's list came from markers the agent itself wrote, so it misses stubs it left unmarked ([Pokémon](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2026-01-25-vjeux-pokemon-showdown-rust.md#what-worked)).
- **VER-8** [stated] Rank failures by cost: no change is cheap, a red change costs an engineer, a green but wrong change costs trust; aim verification at the last kind.
  - Old system as oracle: no. Depends on model ability: no. Strength: medium. Era: 2024–2026; newest: Claude Opus 4.x.
  - Cases: [Spotify: what went wrong](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2025-11-06-spotify-honk.md#what-went-wrong), [GitHub: how it was checked](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2026-09-16-github-copilot-runtime-rust.md#how-it-was-checked), [Zalando: what went wrong](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2025-02-20-zalando-ui-component-libraries.md#what-went-wrong), [Bloomberg: what went wrong](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2026-11-03-bloomberg-python-cpp-uplift.md#what-went-wrong).
  - Against: None found.
- **VER-9** [stated] Where the target has no tests the agent cannot check itself: leave it out, require tests first, or budget for owners to test each change.
  - Old system as oracle: partly. Depends on model ability: no. Strength: weak. Era: 2025–2026; newest: Claude (version unstated).
  - Cases: [Spotify: how it was checked](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2025-11-06-spotify-honk.md#how-it-was-checked), [Spotify: practices to copy](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2025-11-06-spotify-honk.md#practices-to-copy).
  - Against: Intel translated without tests on purpose to measure the repair cost afterwards ([Intel](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2026-08-24-intel-ideas-c-to-rust.md#how-it-was-checked)).
- **VER-10** [stated] Where one change repeats across many targets, keep the pass/fail gates deterministic as the model writes more; an error a model-run gate lets through can spread to every target.
  - Old system as oracle: no. Depends on model ability: partly. Strength: weak. Era: 2025–2026; newest: Claude Opus 4.x.
  - Cases: [Bloomberg: what worked](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2026-11-03-bloomberg-python-cpp-uplift.md#what-worked).
  - Against: Disagree: Google's gates include the model agreeing its change was needed ([Google](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2025-04-13-google-int64-ids.md#how-it-was-checked)), Spotify gates each PR with an LLM judge ([Spotify](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2025-11-06-spotify-honk.md#how-it-was-checked)), Shopify puts two adversarial reviewers (likely agents) on every checkpoint ([Shopify](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2026-09-10-shopify-react-native-to-native.md#how-it-was-checked)), and Bun's reviewer agents, seeing only the diff, caught bugs ([Bun](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2026-07-08-bun-zig-to-rust.md#how-it-was-checked)) and, once a rule was added, rejected stubs ([Bun](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2026-07-08-bun-zig-to-rust.md#what-went-wrong)).
- **VER-11** [stated] Before building the pipeline, judge how late a wrong change first fails; changes that only the owner's deploy could check were merged less and rejected more.
  - Old system as oracle: partly. Depends on model ability: no. Strength: weak. Era: 2025–2026; newest: Claude Opus 4.x.
  - Cases: [Bloomberg: what worked](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2026-11-03-bloomberg-python-cpp-uplift.md#what-worked), [Bloomberg: what went wrong](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2026-11-03-bloomberg-python-cpp-uplift.md#what-went-wrong).
  - Against: None found; Bloomberg's authors cannot separate this from the population, the earlier start, the perceived risk of each move and a part-time review helper ([Bloomberg](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2026-11-03-bloomberg-python-cpp-uplift.md#what-worked)).
- **VER-12** [stated] When the move is done, add a check that stops new code from using the old path, so later work does not quietly undo the migration.
  - Old system as oracle: no. Depends on model ability: no. Strength: weak. Era: 2026; newest: Claude (version unstated).
  - Cases: [GitLab: what worked](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2026-07-08-gitlab-rate-limiting.md#what-worked).
  - Against: None found; one seller's account, which does not say how the check works or whether it has caught anything ([GitLab](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2026-07-08-gitlab-rate-limiting.md#what-went-wrong)).

## Code review (review.md)

How agent-written changes were reviewed, by agents and by people.

- **REV-1** [stated] Never let the writing agent review its own change; use two or more reviewers in fresh contexts that see only the diff and are told to find faults.
  - Old system as oracle: partly. Depends on model ability: partly. Strength: medium. Era: 2026; newest: Claude Opus 5.x.
  - Cases: [Bun: how it was checked](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2026-07-08-bun-zig-to-rust.md#how-it-was-checked), [Bun: what worked](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2026-07-08-bun-zig-to-rust.md#what-worked), [GitHub: practices to copy](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2026-09-16-github-copilot-runtime-rust.md#practices-to-copy), [Ladybird: who did what](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2026-02-23-ladybird-libjs-rust.md#who-did-what), [Mindstone: how it was checked](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2026-07-06-mindstone-go-to-typescript.md#how-it-was-checked).
  - Against: No source measures how much these reviewers miss; an outside critic calls the Bun merge unreviewed ([Bun](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2026-07-08-bun-zig-to-rust.md#what-went-wrong)). At GitLab a change passed an adversarial review agent and Duo Code Review, then broke requests for some users ([GitLab](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2026-07-08-gitlab-rate-limiting.md#what-went-wrong)).
  - Related view (karpathy-ideas): [llm council anonymous peer review](https://github.com/ntroccoli/karpathy-ideas/blob/main/ideas/2025-11-22-llm-council-anonymous-peer-review.md), agrees.
- **REV-2** [stated] Split the review: agents and tests do the exhaustive old-against-new comparison; people spend their attention on architecture, contracts and flagged risk.
  - Old system as oracle: partly. Depends on model ability: partly. Strength: medium. Era: 2026; newest: Claude Opus 5.x.
  - Cases: [GitHub: who did what](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2026-09-16-github-copilot-runtime-rust.md#who-did-what), [Bun: how it was checked](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2026-07-08-bun-zig-to-rust.md#how-it-was-checked).
  - Against: Disagree: at Slack and Google a person checked every change before merge ([Slack](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2024-05-22-slack-enzyme-to-rtl.md#who-did-what)) ([Google](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2025-04-13-google-int64-ids.md#how-it-was-checked)), and Shopify puts a person's approval on every checkpoint ([Shopify](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2026-09-10-shopify-react-native-to-native.md#how-it-was-checked)); in Bun no person read every line. Zalando had a person review every change, and one wrong data change still got through ([Zalando](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2025-02-20-zalando-ui-component-libraries.md#what-went-wrong)). In ts-rust the author says he read none of the code, and no other reviewer is named ([ts-rust](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2026-10-07-ping-tsgo-to-rust.md#who-did-what)).
- **REV-3** [ours] Give reviewers a written list of constructs that read the same in old and new code but behave differently: assertions, eager defaults, falsy checks, number types, built-in validators, equality.
  - Old system as oracle: yes. Depends on model ability: partly. Strength: medium. Era: 2026; newest: Claude Opus 5.x.
  - Cases: [Bun: what went wrong](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2026-07-08-bun-zig-to-rust.md#what-went-wrong), [GitHub: what went wrong](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2026-09-16-github-copilot-runtime-rust.md#what-went-wrong), [Spartacus: what went wrong](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2026-04-13-lutz-leonhardt-spartacus-signal-forms.md#what-went-wrong), [PagerDuty: what went wrong](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2026-04-13-pagerduty-rundeck-grails-7.md#what-went-wrong).
  - Against: None found; the Spartacus post does not say what its reviewer was told to look for ([Spartacus](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2026-04-13-lutz-leonhardt-spartacus-signal-forms.md#what-went-wrong)).
- **REV-4** [stated] Add an automatic scope check that compares each diff with its instruction; agents drift into refactors, switched-off tests and side fixes.
  - Old system as oracle: no. Depends on model ability: partly. Strength: medium. Era: 2025–2026; newest: Claude (version unstated).
  - Cases: [Spotify: what worked](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2025-11-06-spotify-honk.md#what-worked), [Google: how it was checked](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2025-04-13-google-int64-ids.md#how-it-was-checked).
  - Against: Spotify's judge has no evaluation yet, so how often it vetoes good work is unknown ([Spotify](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2025-11-06-spotify-honk.md#what-went-wrong)).
  - Related view (karpathy-ideas): [models too agentic state stakes and scope](https://github.com/ntroccoli/karpathy-ideas/blob/main/ideas/2025-08-09-models-too-agentic-state-stakes-and-scope.md), agrees.
- **REV-5** [ours] Treat LLM reviewers and judges as unmeasured until you know their miss rate; veto counts and showcase catches say nothing about what got through.
  - Old system as oracle: partly. Depends on model ability: no. Strength: medium. Era: 2025–2026; newest: Claude Fable 5.x.
  - Cases: [Spotify: what went wrong](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2025-11-06-spotify-honk.md#what-went-wrong), [Bun: how it was checked](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2026-07-08-bun-zig-to-rust.md#how-it-was-checked), [Spartacus: what went wrong](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2026-04-13-lutz-leonhardt-spartacus-signal-forms.md#what-went-wrong), [GitLab: what went wrong](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2026-07-08-gitlab-rate-limiting.md#what-went-wrong).
  - Against: GitHub turned its session logs into evaluations, a start on measuring ([GitHub](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2026-09-16-github-copilot-runtime-rust.md#what-worked)).
- **REV-6** [stated] Have the tool leave an inline note with a guide link at each spot it deliberately left for a person, so reviewers find the judgement calls fast.
  - Old system as oracle: no. Depends on model ability: no. Strength: medium. Era: 2024–2026; newest: Claude (version unstated).
  - Cases: [Spotify: what worked](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2025-11-06-spotify-honk.md#what-worked), [Slack: who did what](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2024-05-22-slack-enzyme-to-rtl.md#who-did-what).
  - Against: None found.
- **REV-7** [stated] Let people see only changes that already built and passed tests; developers counted that filter as one of the largest gains.
  - Old system as oracle: partly. Depends on model ability: no. Strength: medium. Era: 2025; newest: Gemini (internal).
  - Cases: [Google: what worked](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2025-04-13-google-int64-ids.md#what-worked).
  - Against: The green filter also held back correct changes where old tests already failed ([Google](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2025-04-13-google-int64-ids.md#what-went-wrong)), and a green change can still be wrong in ways reviewers miss ([Spotify](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2025-11-06-spotify-honk.md#what-went-wrong)).
- **REV-8** [stated] Audit the reviewers and the fixer: check that AI reviewers flag real differences and that the agent's answers to review comments hold up.
  - Old system as oracle: partly. Depends on model ability: partly. Strength: medium. Era: 2026; newest: Claude Opus 5.x.
  - Cases: [Bun: how it was checked](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2026-07-08-bun-zig-to-rust.md#how-it-was-checked), [GitHub: what went wrong](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2026-09-16-github-copilot-runtime-rust.md#what-went-wrong).
  - Against: None found.
- **REV-9** [stated] Once agents write fast, review, testing and deploy by the owning teams become the bottleneck; plan for that load from the start: reviewer capacity, evidence that eases review, priority.
  - Old system as oracle: no. Depends on model ability: partly. Strength: strong. Era: 2025–2026; newest: Claude Opus 4.x.
  - Cases: [GitHub: what went wrong](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2026-09-16-github-copilot-runtime-rust.md#what-went-wrong), [Google: who did what](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2025-04-13-google-int64-ids.md#who-did-what), [Spotify: how it was checked](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2025-11-06-spotify-honk.md#how-it-was-checked), [Bloomberg: what went wrong](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2026-11-03-bloomberg-python-cpp-uplift.md#what-went-wrong), [GitLab: what went wrong](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2026-07-08-gitlab-rate-limiting.md#what-went-wrong).
  - Against: At Bloomberg reviewer time was not the whole limit: the moves were low priority and owners carried the deploy risk, so most PRs got no decision; its authors look to more checks inside the pipeline and to runs that owners request ([Bloomberg](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2026-11-03-bloomberg-python-cpp-uplift.md#what-went-wrong)). At Asana, whose engineers reviewed their own agents' pull requests twice a day, slow lint and CI held the work up, not approval ([Asana](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2026-08-07-asana-enzyme-to-rtl.md#what-went-wrong)).
  - Related view (karpathy-ideas): [verification not generation is the bottleneck](https://github.com/ntroccoli/karpathy-ideas/blob/main/ideas/2025-06-04-verification-not-generation-is-the-bottleneck.md), agrees.
- **REV-10** [ours] Grade a small sample of converted code against hand-converted versions with a rubric; pass rates say nothing about readability or idiom.
  - Old system as oracle: no. Depends on model ability: no. Strength: weak. Era: 2024–2026; newest: Claude 2.x.
  - Cases: [Slack: how it was checked](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2024-05-22-slack-enzyme-to-rtl.md#how-it-was-checked), [Ladybird: what went wrong](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2026-02-23-ladybird-libjs-rust.md#what-went-wrong).
  - Against: Airbnb reports intent and coverage kept, with no quality grading ([Airbnb](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2025-04-01-airbnb-enzyme-to-rtl.md#how-it-was-checked)).
- **REV-11** [stated] Code that meets the feature requirements can still duplicate logic, drift from the architecture or run slowly; keep reviewers who know the target platform.
  - Old system as oracle: no. Depends on model ability: partly. Strength: medium. Era: 2025–2026; newest: Claude (version unstated).
  - Cases: [Shopify: what went wrong](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2026-09-10-shopify-react-native-to-native.md#what-went-wrong), [Pokémon: what went wrong](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2026-01-25-vjeux-pokemon-showdown-rust.md#what-went-wrong), [Datadog: what went wrong](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2026-06-23-datadog-foundationdb-to-postgres.md#what-went-wrong).
  - Against: Disagree: in the Pokémon port an engineer who had never written Rust spotted the hard-coded behaviour; only the speed work needed Rust expertise ([Pokémon](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2026-01-25-vjeux-pokemon-showdown-rust.md#what-went-wrong)).

## Release and rollout (rollout.md)

How the new code reached users, and how risk was limited on the way.

- **ROL-1** [stated] Swap one component per change inside normal releases, old and new in one tree joined by a temporary bridge, so the main branch can always ship.
  - Old system as oracle: partly. Depends on model ability: no. Strength: medium. Era: 2025–2026; newest: Claude Opus 5.x.
  - Cases: [GitHub: what worked](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2026-09-16-github-copilot-runtime-rust.md#what-worked), [GitHub: practices to copy](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2026-09-16-github-copilot-runtime-rust.md#practices-to-copy), [Uber: what worked](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2026-04-07-uber-junit4-to-junit5.md#what-worked), [Ladybird: what was migrated](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2026-02-23-ladybird-libjs-rust.md#what-was-migrated).
  - Against: Disagree: Bun's author says doing everything at once beats an incremental move, and merged one branch after eleven days ([Bun](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2026-07-08-bun-zig-to-rust.md#what-worked)); Shopify chose a fresh native build over a gradual move inside the old app ([Shopify](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2026-09-10-shopify-react-native-to-native.md#what-was-migrated)) and shipped it after about two months of beta ([Shopify](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2026-09-10-shopify-react-native-to-native.md#how-it-was-checked)); Mindstone rejected a service-by-service move as likely to stall and moved all its services in about two weeks ([Mindstone](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2026-07-06-mindstone-go-to-typescript.md#what-worked)).
- **ROL-2** [stated] Treat merged and released as separate gates: ship first to a canary or pre-release that few users take, and promote it only after real use.
  - Old system as oracle: no. Depends on model ability: no. Strength: medium. Era: 2025–2026; newest: Claude Opus 5.x.
  - Cases: [Bun: what went wrong](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2026-07-08-bun-zig-to-rust.md#what-went-wrong), [GitHub: how it was checked](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2026-09-16-github-copilot-runtime-rust.md#how-it-was-checked), [Google: what went wrong](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2025-04-13-google-int64-ids.md#what-went-wrong), [Checkly: what worked](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2026-09-01-checkly-nodejs-to-go.md#what-worked).
  - Against: Some GitHub regressions still reached a stable release ([GitHub](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2026-09-16-github-copilot-runtime-rust.md#how-it-was-checked)). GitLab ramped a cohort to full traffic while its shadow comparison flagged a divergence that its labels did not single out ([GitLab](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2026-07-08-gitlab-rate-limiting.md#what-went-wrong)).
- **ROL-3** [stated] Changes that reach many teams' systems still need slow production rollouts watched by their owners; the AI pipeline speeds the code, not this step.
  - Old system as oracle: no. Depends on model ability: no. Strength: medium. Era: 2025–2026; newest: Claude Opus 4.x.
  - Cases: [Google: what went wrong](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2025-04-13-google-int64-ids.md#what-went-wrong), [Bloomberg: what went wrong](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2026-11-03-bloomberg-python-cpp-uplift.md#what-went-wrong), [GitLab: what went wrong](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2026-07-08-gitlab-rate-limiting.md#what-went-wrong).
  - Against: A downstream product took the whole Bun rewrite in one release and barely anyone noticed ([Bun](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2026-07-08-bun-zig-to-rust.md#what-went-wrong)).
- **ROL-4** [stated] Delete the old code in the same change that adds the new; concurrent edits to ported code then surface as rebase conflicts instead of silent losses.
  - Old system as oracle: no. Depends on model ability: no. Strength: weak. Era: 2026; newest: Claude Opus 5.x.
  - Cases: [GitHub: how it was checked](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2026-09-16-github-copilot-runtime-rust.md#how-it-was-checked).
  - Against: Branch drift and rebases still caused a few regressions ([GitHub](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2026-09-16-github-copilot-runtime-rust.md#what-went-wrong)).
- **ROL-5** [stated] Keep agent branches short-lived against a busy main branch; sessions left open for days pile up drift, and rebases lose changes.
  - Old system as oracle: no. Depends on model ability: partly. Strength: weak. Era: 2026; newest: Claude Opus 5.x.
  - Cases: [GitHub: what went wrong](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2026-09-16-github-copilot-runtime-rust.md#what-went-wrong).
  - Against: None found.
- **ROL-6** [ours] Track the size of the temporary bridge between old and new as the progress signal and drive it to zero; line counts on a busy code base mislead.
  - Old system as oracle: no. Depends on model ability: no. Strength: weak. Era: 2026; newest: Claude Opus 5.x.
  - Cases: [GitHub: numbers](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2026-09-16-github-copilot-runtime-rust.md#numbers).
  - Against: None found.
- **ROL-7** [stated] Ship a new failure boundary (such as hosting in-process) as an opt-in mode beside the old default, separate from the code port itself.
  - Old system as oracle: partly. Depends on model ability: no. Strength: weak. Era: 2026; newest: Claude Opus 5.x.
  - Cases: [GitHub: how it was checked](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2026-09-16-github-copilot-runtime-rust.md#how-it-was-checked).
  - Against: None found.
- **ROL-8** [stated] When old and new run side by side, send a unit that fails its tests back to the old framework rather than block the rollout or diagnose each failure.
  - Old system as oracle: yes. Depends on model ability: no. Strength: weak. Era: 2025–2026; newest: unstated.
  - Cases: [Uber: what went wrong](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2026-04-07-uber-junit4-to-junit5.md#what-went-wrong), [Uber: what worked](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2026-04-07-uber-junit4-to-junit5.md#what-worked).
  - Against: None found; Uber does not say how many units stayed on the old framework ([Uber](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2026-04-07-uber-junit4-to-junit5.md#what-went-wrong)).
- **ROL-9** [stated] Unrequested changes of low priority mostly sit undecided; let owners commit to the generated branch, and consider generating hard-to-check moves only when owners ask.
  - Old system as oracle: no. Depends on model ability: no. Strength: weak. Era: 2025–2026; newest: Claude Opus 4.x.
  - Cases: [Bloomberg: what went wrong](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2026-11-03-bloomberg-python-cpp-uplift.md#what-went-wrong).
  - Against: None found; both remedies are plans the authors have not yet tried.
- **ROL-10** [stated] Shadow agreement on light traffic proves little: aim the old-against-new comparison at the largest and oddest inputs, check each answer is possible at all, and label mismatches by kind.
  - Old system as oracle: partly. Depends on model ability: no. Strength: medium. Era: 2026; newest: Claude (version unstated).
  - Cases: [GitLab: what worked](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2026-07-08-gitlab-rate-limiting.md#what-worked), [GitLab: what went wrong](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2026-07-08-gitlab-rate-limiting.md#what-went-wrong), [Temporal: what worked](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2026-09-02-temporal-billing-store-clickhouse.md#what-worked), [Temporal: how it was checked](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2026-09-02-temporal-billing-store-clickhouse.md#how-it-was-checked).
  - Against: None found; GitLab is a seller's account that shows no data, and Temporal reports one defect and does not say whether agents wrote the query that overflowed ([Temporal](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2026-09-02-temporal-billing-store-clickhouse.md#what-went-wrong)).
- **ROL-11** [stated] Cut over in order of how costly a mistake is to undo, often against the direction data flows: read-only paths first, paths whose output leaves the system last, each behind a flag.
  - Old system as oracle: no. Depends on model ability: no. Strength: weak. Era: 2026; newest: unstated.
  - Cases: [Temporal: what worked](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2026-09-02-temporal-billing-store-clickhouse.md#what-worked), [Temporal: how it was checked](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2026-09-02-temporal-billing-store-clickhouse.md#how-it-was-checked).
  - Against: None found; one company's account, and it does not report how often the flag was used to roll back ([Temporal](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2026-09-02-temporal-billing-store-clickhouse.md#what-went-wrong)).

## Machines and operations (operations.md)

Running many agents on real machines, and keeping the result healthy after merge.

- **OPS-1** [stated] Parallel agents saturate CPU, disk and I/O: size the machine first, let one agent build at a time through a lease, and push full test runs to CI.
  - Old system as oracle: no. Depends on model ability: no. Strength: medium. Era: 2026; newest: Claude Opus 5.x.
  - Cases: [GitHub: what went wrong](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2026-09-16-github-copilot-runtime-rust.md#what-went-wrong), [Bun: what went wrong](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2026-07-08-bun-zig-to-rust.md#what-went-wrong).
  - Against: At Asana, CI results that differed from local checks, with a slow lint step, were where people had to step in most ([Asana](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2026-08-07-asana-enzyme-to-rtl.md#what-went-wrong)): pushing runs to CI helps only if CI matches local runs.
- **OPS-2** [stated] Contain heavy tests with operating-system limits (control groups, process namespaces, disk quotas); asking the agent to be careful contains nothing.
  - Old system as oracle: no. Depends on model ability: partly. Strength: weak. Era: 2026; newest: Claude Fable 5.x.
