  - Cases: [Bun: what went wrong](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2026-07-08-bun-zig-to-rust.md#what-went-wrong), [Spartacus: what went wrong](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2026-04-13-lutz-leonhardt-spartacus-signal-forms.md#what-went-wrong).
  - Against: Bun's limits covered memory, CPU and processes, yet the disk still filled and crashed the machine several times ([Bun](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2026-07-08-bun-zig-to-rust.md#what-went-wrong)); no case shows disk quotas in use.
- **OPS-3** [stated] Make the inner loop fast (module splits, build caches, host I/O) before scaling agents; their time goes mostly to reading, building and testing, not writing.
  - Old system as oracle: no. Depends on model ability: partly. Strength: strong. Era: 2025–2026; newest: Claude Opus 5.x.
  - Cases: [GitHub: what went wrong](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2026-09-16-github-copilot-runtime-rust.md#what-went-wrong), [GitHub: numbers](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2026-09-16-github-copilot-runtime-rust.md#numbers), [Bun: practices to copy](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2026-07-08-bun-zig-to-rust.md#practices-to-copy), [Shopify: what went wrong](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2026-09-10-shopify-react-native-to-native.md#what-went-wrong), [Asana: what went wrong](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2026-08-07-asana-enzyme-to-rtl.md#what-went-wrong), [Mindstone: what worked](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2026-07-06-mindstone-go-to-typescript.md#what-worked).
  - Against: At Shopify the slow step was not the build: hot reload helped but did not fix it, because agents read and drove the app through simulators; its fix is a headless path into the app's logic ([Shopify](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2026-09-10-shopify-react-native-to-native.md#what-worked)).
- **OPS-4** [stated] List what the old runtime supplied silently (time zone, environment, process flags) and test every platform you ship; one green platform says little.
  - Old system as oracle: yes. Depends on model ability: no. Strength: medium. Era: 2025–2026; newest: Claude Opus 5.x.
  - Cases: [GitHub: what went wrong](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2026-09-16-github-copilot-runtime-rust.md#what-went-wrong), [Spotify: what went wrong](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2025-11-06-spotify-honk.md#what-went-wrong).
  - Against: None found.
- **OPS-5** [stated] Keep hardening after merge: repeated security review, round-the-clock fuzzing and leak tracking, with people reviewing the fixes they produce.
  - Old system as oracle: no. Depends on model ability: no. Strength: weak. Era: 2026; newest: Claude Fable 5.x.
  - Cases: [Bun: how it was checked](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2026-07-08-bun-zig-to-rust.md#how-it-was-checked).
  - Against: Disagree: the Zig creator says Bun was not fuzzing before the port, against the post's claim ([Bun](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2026-07-08-bun-zig-to-rust.md#what-went-wrong)).
- **OPS-6** [stated] Run bulk change jobs, by agent or by rule, as scheduled batches sized to the infrastructure, sort results into status groups, and rerun only what is stuck.
  - Old system as oracle: partly. Depends on model ability: no. Strength: strong. Era: 2024–2026; newest: Gemini (internal).
  - Cases: [Slack: what worked](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2024-05-22-slack-enzyme-to-rtl.md#what-worked), [Google: what worked](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2025-04-13-google-int64-ids.md#what-worked), [Airbnb: what worked](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2025-04-01-airbnb-enzyme-to-rtl.md#what-worked), [Uber: what worked](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2026-04-07-uber-junit4-to-junit5.md#what-worked).
  - Against: Batches sized to the infrastructure can still outrun the people receiving them: Bloomberg's PRs went out in a few bursts while merges came at a steady rate of their own ([Bloomberg](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2026-11-03-bloomberg-python-cpp-uplift.md#what-went-wrong)).
- **OPS-7** [ours] Load-test the new code for blocking and resource exhaustion; one port froze its interface on a synchronous call across the bridge.
  - Old system as oracle: partly. Depends on model ability: no. Strength: medium. Era: 2026; newest: Claude Opus 5.x.
  - Cases: [GitHub: what went wrong](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2026-09-16-github-copilot-runtime-rust.md#what-went-wrong).
  - Against: None found.
- **OPS-8** [ours] Check the headroom of shared services old and new paths both hit, such as caches and rate-limit stores; one team's store lacked room for double load, and raising it took infrastructure work.
  - Old system as oracle: no. Depends on model ability: no. Strength: weak. Era: 2026; newest: Claude (version unstated).
  - Cases: [GitLab: what went wrong](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2026-07-08-gitlab-rate-limiting.md#what-went-wrong).
  - Against: None found; one case, its limit was known before the migration began, and the source does not say the side-by-side running brought it back.

## Security (security.md)

Sandboxing agents, memory safety, dependencies and data integrity.

- **SEC-1** [stated] Run unattended agents in a minimal sandbox with an allowlist of commands; pushing, merging and talking to people belong to the surrounding infrastructure.
  - Old system as oracle: no. Depends on model ability: partly. Strength: weak. Era: 2025–2026; newest: Claude (version unstated).
  - Cases: [Spotify: what worked](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2025-11-06-spotify-honk.md#what-worked), [Spotify: practices to copy](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2025-11-06-spotify-honk.md#practices-to-copy).
  - Against: Bun's agents committed and pushed themselves and the project still finished ([Bun](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2026-07-08-bun-zig-to-rust.md#what-went-wrong)). One author found the sandbox blocked pushing and an antivirus stopped each new build, and worked around both (a local server running git, builds in Docker, every prompt approved) to keep his agent running; he reports no harm ([Pokémon](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2026-01-25-vjeux-pokemon-showdown-rust.md#what-went-wrong)).
  - Related view (karpathy-ideas): [agent security is the wild west](https://github.com/ntroccoli/karpathy-ideas/blob/main/ideas/2025-06-16-agent-security-is-the-wild-west.md), agrees.
- **SEC-2** [stated] Whatever the harness exposes may get used unasked (an unlisted skill, git commands, a peer's worktree); remove what the task does not need.
  - Old system as oracle: no. Depends on model ability: partly. Strength: medium. Era: 2025–2026; newest: Claude Opus 5.x.
  - Cases: [GitHub: what went wrong](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2026-09-16-github-copilot-runtime-rust.md#what-went-wrong), [Bun: what went wrong](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2026-07-08-bun-zig-to-rust.md#what-went-wrong), [Spotify: what worked](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2025-11-06-spotify-honk.md#what-worked).
  - Against: Disagree: Spotify itself is adding skills and self-gathered context because prompts grew unwieldy without them ([Spotify](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2025-11-06-spotify-honk.md#what-went-wrong)).
- **SEC-3** [ours] Block destructive repository and system commands in the tool layer, not with a prompt rule, which only arrives after the damage.
  - Old system as oracle: no. Depends on model ability: partly. Strength: medium. Era: 2025–2026; newest: Claude Fable 5.x.
  - Cases: [Bun: what went wrong](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2026-07-08-bun-zig-to-rust.md#what-went-wrong), [Spotify: practices to copy](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2025-11-06-spotify-honk.md#practices-to-copy).
  - Against: None found; one author ran an agent for weeks on his own computer with every prompt approved by a key-press script and reports no damage ([Pokémon](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2026-01-25-vjeux-pokemon-showdown-rust.md#what-went-wrong)); one unharmed run is a small sample.
- **SEC-4** [stated] After a port into a memory-safe language, count where unsafe code sits, allow it only at foreign and system boundaries, and have the compiler forbid it elsewhere.
  - Old system as oracle: no. Depends on model ability: no. Strength: medium. Era: 2026; newest: Claude Opus 5.x.
  - Cases: [GitHub: numbers](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2026-09-16-github-copilot-runtime-rust.md#numbers), [Bun: what went wrong](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2026-07-08-bun-zig-to-rust.md#what-went-wrong), [Intel: practices to copy](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2026-08-24-intel-ideas-c-to-rust.md#practices-to-copy).
  - Against: Disagree: on how much to allow, Bun's faithful port keeps far more unsafe code and plans to cut it only by later refactoring ([Bun](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2026-07-08-bun-zig-to-rust.md#what-went-wrong)).
- **SEC-5** [stated] Generate foreign-function signatures with a binding tool and reject any model answer that differs; a wrong contract leaks unsafety into safe-looking code.
  - Old system as oracle: partly. Depends on model ability: partly. Strength: medium. Era: 2026; newest: GPT-5.x.
  - Cases: [Intel: what worked](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2026-08-24-intel-ideas-c-to-rust.md#what-worked), [Intel: practices to copy](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2026-08-24-intel-ideas-c-to-rust.md#practices-to-copy).
  - Against: None found.
- **SEC-6** [ours] A bounds-checked target turns silent out-of-range access into crashes; expect new crash reports and test limits at real-world sizes.
  - Old system as oracle: partly. Depends on model ability: no. Strength: medium. Era: 2026; newest: Claude Fable 5.x.
  - Cases: [Bun: what went wrong](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2026-07-08-bun-zig-to-rust.md#what-went-wrong).
  - Against: None found.
- **SEC-7** [ours] Treat each replaced library as a migration of its own, above all sanitizers, credential stores and protocol SDKs, and vet every new dependency.
  - Old system as oracle: partly. Depends on model ability: no. Strength: medium. Era: 2026; newest: Claude Opus 5.x.
  - Cases: [GitHub: what went wrong](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2026-09-16-github-copilot-runtime-rust.md#what-went-wrong).
  - Against: None found; no case shows new dependencies being vetted.
  - Related view (karpathy-ideas): [rethink dependencies supply chain](https://github.com/ntroccoli/karpathy-ideas/blob/main/ideas/2026-03-24-rethink-dependencies-supply-chain.md), agrees.
- **SEC-8** [stated] Treat agent session logs and traces as data that may hold secrets; control where they are stored and where they are uploaded.
  - Old system as oracle: no. Depends on model ability: no. Strength: medium. Era: 2025–2026; newest: Claude Opus 5.x.
  - Cases: [GitHub: how it was checked](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2026-09-16-github-copilot-runtime-rust.md#how-it-was-checked), [Spotify: who did what](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2025-11-06-spotify-honk.md#who-did-what).
  - Against: None found.
- **SEC-9** [stated] Isolate each agent run from earlier attempts and reference answers, which it could otherwise read and lean on; decide about network access too.
  - Old system as oracle: no. Depends on model ability: partly. Strength: weak. Era: 2025–2026; newest: Claude Opus 4.x.
  - Cases: [Intel: who did what](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2026-08-24-intel-ideas-c-to-rust.md#who-did-what), [Bloomberg: who did what](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2026-11-03-bloomberg-python-cpp-uplift.md#who-did-what).
  - Against: None found.
- **SEC-10** [stated] Never let agents choose the order of schema changes, backfills or ownership of shared tables; one agent's chosen order would have lost data silently.
  - Old system as oracle: no. Depends on model ability: partly. Strength: weak. Era: 2026; newest: unstated.
  - Cases: [1Password: what went wrong](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2026-04-20-1password-monolith-refactor.md#what-went-wrong), [1Password: practices to copy](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2026-04-20-1password-monolith-refactor.md#practices-to-copy).
  - Against: None found.

## Cost (cost.md)

Tokens, money, people's time and the bill after merge.

- **CST-1** [stated] Long agent runs are affordable only with high prompt-cache reuse: keep a stable prompt prefix and track the hit rate and each kind of token.
  - Old system as oracle: no. Depends on model ability: no. Strength: medium. Era: 2026; newest: Claude Opus 5.x.
  - Cases: [GitHub: numbers](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2026-09-16-github-copilot-runtime-rust.md#numbers), [GitHub: what worked](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2026-09-16-github-copilot-runtime-rust.md#what-worked), [Bun: numbers](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2026-07-08-bun-zig-to-rust.md#numbers).
  - Against: With a model call per file, Zalando put its API bill under $40 per repository before any cache discount ([Zalando](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2025-02-20-zalando-ui-component-libraries.md#numbers)); the cache matters most for long agent runs. Zalando still ordered its prompt for caching ([Zalando](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2025-02-20-zalando-ui-component-libraries.md#what-worked)).
- **CST-2** [ours] Ask for the full bill: tokens at the price paid, people's hours by role, compute and CI, review, and the work after merge; most sources give one piece.
  - Old system as oracle: no. Depends on model ability: no. Strength: strong. Era: 2024–2026; newest: GPT-6.x.
  - Cases: [GitHub: numbers](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2026-09-16-github-copilot-runtime-rust.md#numbers), [Bun: numbers](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2026-07-08-bun-zig-to-rust.md#numbers), [Airbnb: what went wrong](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2025-04-01-airbnb-enzyme-to-rtl.md#what-went-wrong), [Spotify: what went wrong](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2025-11-06-spotify-honk.md#what-went-wrong), [ts-rust: numbers](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2026-10-07-ping-tsgo-to-rust.md#numbers), [PagerDuty: what went wrong](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2026-04-13-pagerduty-rundeck-grails-7.md#what-went-wrong).
  - Against: GitHub gives the fullest token breakdown in the set ([GitHub](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2026-09-16-github-copilot-runtime-rust.md#numbers)).
- **CST-3** [ours] Expect cost per unit to have a long tail; report median and mean, and size the budget for hub components and hard files.
  - Old system as oracle: no. Depends on model ability: no. Strength: medium. Era: 2024–2026; newest: Claude Opus 5.x.
  - Cases: [Intel: what worked](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2026-08-24-intel-ideas-c-to-rust.md#what-worked), [GitHub: numbers](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2026-09-16-github-copilot-runtime-rust.md#numbers), [Airbnb: what went wrong](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2025-04-01-airbnb-enzyme-to-rtl.md#what-went-wrong).
  - Against: None found.
- **CST-4** [ours] Before reusing a published cost, check the model, how it was reached and the price basis; pre-release, internal or partner models give costs others cannot repeat.
  - Old system as oracle: no. Depends on model ability: no. Strength: medium. Era: 2025–2026; newest: GPT-6.x.
  - Cases: [Bun: who did what](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2026-07-08-bun-zig-to-rust.md#who-did-what), [Intel: who did what](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2026-08-24-intel-ideas-c-to-rust.md#who-did-what), [Google: who did what](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2025-04-13-google-int64-ids.md#who-did-what), [Asana: source](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2026-08-07-asana-enzyme-to-rtl.md#source), [ts-rust: numbers](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2026-10-07-ping-tsgo-to-rust.md#numbers).
  - Against: None found.
- **CST-5** [ours] Work out cost per unit inside one case and name the unit; added lines, production lines, symbols and files differ, and tokens do not convert to money across cases.
  - Old system as oracle: no. Depends on model ability: no. Strength: medium. Era: 2026; newest: Claude Opus 5.x.
  - Cases: [Bun: numbers](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2026-07-08-bun-zig-to-rust.md#numbers), [GitHub: numbers](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2026-09-16-github-copilot-runtime-rust.md#numbers), [Intel: numbers](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2026-08-24-intel-ideas-c-to-rust.md#numbers).
  - Against: None found.
- **CST-6** [ours] Count the work after merge (regression fixes, security rounds, fuzzing, clean-up and speed work) in what the migration cost.
  - Old system as oracle: no. Depends on model ability: no. Strength: medium. Era: 2026; newest: Claude Opus 5.x.
  - Cases: [Bun: what went wrong](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2026-07-08-bun-zig-to-rust.md#what-went-wrong), [GitHub: what went wrong](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2026-09-16-github-copilot-runtime-rust.md#what-went-wrong).
  - Against: None found.
- **CST-7** [ours] Budget review agents as a multiple of generation (several reviewers and a fixer per writer), and ask for their share of tokens, which no case reports.
  - Old system as oracle: no. Depends on model ability: no. Strength: medium. Era: 2026; newest: Claude Opus 5.x.
  - Cases: [Bun: who did what](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2026-07-08-bun-zig-to-rust.md#who-did-what), [GitHub: practices to copy](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2026-09-16-github-copilot-runtime-rust.md#practices-to-copy).
  - Against: None found.
- **CST-8** [stated] Missing or broken tests in target repositories, or checks the pipeline cannot run, shift the cost of checking onto the teams that receive the changes; the central figures leave it out.
  - Old system as oracle: partly. Depends on model ability: no. Strength: medium. Era: 2025–2026; newest: Claude Opus 4.x.
  - Cases: [Spotify: how it was checked](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2025-11-06-spotify-honk.md#how-it-was-checked), [Google: what went wrong](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2025-04-13-google-int64-ids.md#what-went-wrong), [Bloomberg: what went wrong](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2026-11-03-bloomberg-python-cpp-uplift.md#what-went-wrong).
  - Against: None found.
- **CST-9** [ours] Pipeline and harness costs pay back over many repositories or migrations; a one-off project should reuse a general harness rather than build one.
  - Old system as oracle: no. Depends on model ability: no. Strength: weak. Era: 2025–2026; newest: Claude (version unstated).
  - Cases: [Spotify: numbers](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2025-11-06-spotify-honk.md#numbers), [Spotify: what worked](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2025-11-06-spotify-honk.md#what-worked).
  - Against: Disagree: Airbnb built its own pipeline for one migration and finished far inside its manual estimate ([Airbnb](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2025-04-01-airbnb-enzyme-to-rtl.md#who-did-what)), and Slack's author expects custom pipelines to stay necessary ([Slack](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2024-05-22-slack-enzyme-to-rtl.md#what-went-wrong)).

## Team and roles (team.md)

Who does what when agents write most of the code.

- **TEM-1** [stated] The lead engineer's job becomes running the control loop: framing slices, challenging design, pushing for completeness, deciding every merge.
  - Old system as oracle: no. Depends on model ability: partly. Strength: medium. Era: 2025–2026; newest: Claude Opus 5.x.
  - Cases: [GitHub: numbers](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2026-09-16-github-copilot-runtime-rust.md#numbers), [GitHub: who did what](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2026-09-16-github-copilot-runtime-rust.md#who-did-what), [Bun: who did what](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2026-07-08-bun-zig-to-rust.md#who-did-what), [Pokémon: who did what](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2026-01-25-vjeux-pokemon-showdown-rust.md#who-did-what), [Ladybird: who did what](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2026-02-23-ladybird-libjs-rust.md#who-did-what).
  - Against: GitHub's split of the engineer's messages by intent was labelled by an LLM, not checked by a person ([GitHub](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2026-09-16-github-copilot-runtime-rust.md#numbers)). At PagerDuty a product manager, not an engineer, ran the loop and approved each fix, and engineers reviewed and finished the work ([PagerDuty](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2026-04-13-pagerduty-rundeck-grails-7.md#who-did-what)).
  - Related view (karpathy-ideas): [partial autonomy and autonomy slider](https://github.com/ntroccoli/karpathy-ideas/blob/main/ideas/2025-06-17-partial-autonomy-and-autonomy-slider.md), agrees.
- **TEM-2** [stated] Count the people behind a one-engineer story (reviewers in many teams, interop, packaging and build specialists) and staff and budget for them.
  - Old system as oracle: no. Depends on model ability: no. Strength: strong. Era: 2024–2026; newest: Claude Opus 5.x.
  - Cases: [GitHub: who did what](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2026-09-16-github-copilot-runtime-rust.md#who-did-what), [Google: who did what](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2025-04-13-google-int64-ids.md#who-did-what), [Slack: who did what](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2024-05-22-slack-enzyme-to-rtl.md#who-did-what), [PagerDuty: who did what](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2026-04-13-pagerduty-rundeck-grails-7.md#who-did-what).
  - Against: Bun credits the port to one engineer and names no helpers for it ([Bun](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2026-07-08-bun-zig-to-rust.md#who-did-what)), and the Pokémon Showdown port was one person's holiday project ([Pokémon](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2026-01-25-vjeux-pokemon-showdown-rust.md#who-did-what)).
- **TEM-3** [stated] A central team should own the agent tooling, build it with early adopters, and teach prompt writing; untrained users fell into the same traps.
  - Old system as oracle: no. Depends on model ability: partly. Strength: medium. Era: 2024–2026; newest: Claude (version unstated).
  - Cases: [Spotify: who did what](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2025-11-06-spotify-honk.md#who-did-what), [Spotify: what went wrong](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2025-11-06-spotify-honk.md#what-went-wrong), [Slack: who did what](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2024-05-22-slack-enzyme-to-rtl.md#who-did-what).
  - Against: None found.
- **TEM-4** [stated] Review in two tiers: the migration owner screens each batch, then code owners accept; expect the load to spread over many teams.
  - Old system as oracle: no. Depends on model ability: no. Strength: medium. Era: 2025–2026; newest: Claude Opus 4.x.
  - Cases: [Google: how it was checked](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2025-04-13-google-int64-ids.md#how-it-was-checked), [Spotify: who did what](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2025-11-06-spotify-honk.md#who-did-what), [Bloomberg: who did what](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2026-11-03-bloomberg-python-cpp-uplift.md#who-did-what).
  - Against: In Bun one engineer merged alone, with no second tier ([Bun](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2026-07-08-bun-zig-to-rust.md#who-did-what)).
- **TEM-5** [stated] Code the model migrates is code the team never wrote; keep owners close to it and teach them the new library, or debugging and incident handling suffer.
  - Old system as oracle: no. Depends on model ability: no. Strength: weak. Era: 2024–2025; newest: GPT-4o.
  - Cases: [Zalando: what went wrong](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2025-02-20-zalando-ui-component-libraries.md#what-went-wrong).
  - Against: ts-rust's author says he read none of the ported code and left the fixing to agents; it reports no incident either way, so the case neither shows nor rules out the cost ([ts-rust](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2026-10-07-ping-tsgo-to-rust.md#who-did-what)). In the Pokémon port the agent debugged on its own though the owner had never written Rust; the one gap he reports was in judging speed work ([Pokémon](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2026-01-25-vjeux-pokemon-showdown-rust.md#what-went-wrong)).
- **TEM-6** [stated] Budget for the people: an engineer new to agents can loop with one without progress, and steering agents that cut corners, then reviewing all they produce, drains the people doing it.
  - Old system as oracle: no. Depends on model ability: partly. Strength: weak. Era: 2026; newest: Claude (version unstated).
  - Cases: [Mindstone: what went wrong](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2026-07-06-mindstone-go-to-typescript.md#what-went-wrong), [GitLab: what went wrong](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2026-07-08-gitlab-rate-limiting.md#what-went-wrong).
  - Against: None found; neither case gives hours, headcount or review load, and GitLab's is one engineer's remark in a seller's account ([Mindstone](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2026-07-06-mindstone-go-to-typescript.md#what-went-wrong), [GitLab](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2026-07-08-gitlab-rate-limiting.md#what-went-wrong)).

## Rule-based tools and AI (tooling.md)

Splitting the work between deterministic tools and models.

- **TOL-1** [stated] Have agents build deterministic tools (analysers, call-site manifests, porting guides, ownership tables), review those, then bind later agent work to them.
  - Old system as oracle: no. Depends on model ability: partly. Strength: strong. Era: 2025–2026; newest: GPT-5.x.
  - Cases: [1Password: what worked](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2026-04-20-1password-monolith-refactor.md#what-worked), [Bun: what worked](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2026-07-08-bun-zig-to-rust.md#what-worked), [Intel: who did what](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2026-08-24-intel-ideas-c-to-rust.md#who-did-what), [Pokémon: what worked](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2026-01-25-vjeux-pokemon-showdown-rust.md#what-worked).
  - Against: Ordering errors persisted at 1Password even with explicit rules in place ([1Password](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2026-04-20-1password-monolith-refactor.md#what-went-wrong)).
- **TOL-2** [stated] Run a rule-based codemod first and give the model its partial output, with a note wherever the rules gave up; it anchors the model.
  - Old system as oracle: partly. Depends on model ability: yes. Strength: medium. Era: 2024–2025; newest: Gemini (internal).
  - Cases: [Slack: what worked](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2024-05-22-slack-enzyme-to-rtl.md#what-worked), [Google: who did what](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2025-04-13-google-int64-ids.md#who-did-what).
  - Against: Uber's recipes made all its rewrites with no model step, and its attempt to have AI migrate several files at once failed ([Uber](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2026-04-07-uber-junit4-to-junit5.md#who-did-what)).
- **TOL-3** [stated] Find change sites with a code index or static analysis, include too many rather than too few, and let the model edit the whole file around each hint.
  - Old system as oracle: partly. Depends on model ability: partly. Strength: medium. Era: 2025–2026; newest: Gemini (internal).
  - Cases: [Google: what worked](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2025-04-13-google-int64-ids.md#what-worked), [1Password: what worked](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2026-04-20-1password-monolith-refactor.md#what-worked).
  - Against: The index can miss sites beyond its hop limit ([Google](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2025-04-13-google-int64-ids.md#what-went-wrong)).
- **TOL-4** [stated] Price the rule-based alternative with the upkeep of its rules; hand-written transforms keep growing on long-tail patterns, which is where models pay off.
  - Old system as oracle: no. Depends on model ability: partly. Strength: medium. Era: 2024–2026; newest: Claude (version unstated).
  - Cases: [Spotify: numbers](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2025-11-06-spotify-honk.md#numbers), [Slack: what went wrong](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2024-05-22-slack-enzyme-to-rtl.md#what-went-wrong), [Google: what worked](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2025-04-13-google-int64-ids.md#what-worked), [Zalando: what worked](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2025-02-20-zalando-ui-component-libraries.md#what-worked).
  - Against: Disagree: Uber kept writing recipes for each common build failure and sent failing files back to the old framework, so rules alone carried its long tail while a model attempt failed ([Uber](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2026-04-07-uber-junit4-to-junit5.md#what-went-wrong)). At Slack the codemod's output still steered the model better than prompt work ([Slack](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2024-05-22-slack-enzyme-to-rtl.md#what-worked)), so rules stay in the system.
- **TOL-5** [stated] Keep agents and models behind your own thin interface, log traces from day one, and pin model and settings per run; the best agent changed within a year.
  - Old system as oracle: no. Depends on model ability: partly. Strength: medium. Era: 2025–2026; newest: Claude (version unstated).
  - Cases: [Spotify: what worked](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2025-11-06-spotify-honk.md#what-worked), [Google: who did what](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2025-04-13-google-int64-ids.md#who-did-what).
  - Against: Disagree: GitHub switched models per slice and mid-session, trading repeatability for fit ([GitHub](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2026-09-16-github-copilot-runtime-rust.md#what-worked)).
  - Related view (karpathy-ideas): [plan for intelligence brownouts](https://github.com/ntroccoli/karpathy-ideas/blob/main/ideas/2026-03-11-plan-for-intelligence-brownouts.md), agrees.
- **TOL-6** [stated] Set up linters, formatters, type checks and coding instructions before the first change, and run them inside the agent's loop, not only in CI.
  - Old system as oracle: no. Depends on model ability: partly. Strength: strong. Era: 2024–2026; newest: Claude Opus 5.x.
  - Cases: [GitHub: what worked](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2026-09-16-github-copilot-runtime-rust.md#what-worked), [Spotify: practices to copy](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2025-11-06-spotify-honk.md#practices-to-copy), [Airbnb: what worked](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2025-04-01-airbnb-enzyme-to-rtl.md#what-worked), [Slack: what worked](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2024-05-22-slack-enzyme-to-rtl.md#what-worked), [Temporal: what went wrong](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2026-09-02-temporal-billing-store-clickhouse.md#what-went-wrong).
  - Against: At Shopify, with guidance, linting, tests and static analysis in place, generated code could still repeat logic or drift from the architecture, so native experts stayed essential ([Shopify](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2026-09-10-shopify-react-native-to-native.md#what-went-wrong)).
  - Related view (karpathy-ideas): [agents ignore code style rules](https://github.com/ntroccoli/karpathy-ideas/blob/main/ideas/2026-03-21-agents-ignore-code-style-rules.md), agrees.
- **TOL-7** [stated] Before choosing a model for a mechanical framework move, try deterministic rewrites on a typed syntax tree; at very large scale they were judged more practical.
  - Old system as oracle: partly. Depends on model ability: partly. Strength: weak. Era: 2025–2026; newest: unstated.
  - Cases: [Uber: what went wrong](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2026-04-07-uber-junit4-to-junit5.md#what-went-wrong), [Uber: what worked](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2026-04-07-uber-junit4-to-junit5.md#what-worked).
  - Against: Slack's codemod alone left work that a model then finished ([Slack](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2024-05-22-slack-enzyme-to-rtl.md#what-worked)); Airbnb's LLM pipeline moved a test framework with no rule-based core ([Airbnb](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2025-04-01-airbnb-enzyme-to-rtl.md#what-worked)).
- **TOL-8** [stated] Give agents a direct way to inspect and drive the running app (state, events, commands, logic run headless); screenshots and accessibility trees made each test take minutes.
  - Old system as oracle: partly. Depends on model ability: partly. Strength: weak. Era: 2025–2026; newest: unstated.
  - Cases: [Shopify: what went wrong](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2026-09-10-shopify-react-native-to-native.md#what-went-wrong), [Shopify: what worked](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2026-09-10-shopify-react-native-to-native.md#what-worked).
  - Against: None found; Shopify gives no measured result for its headless CLI ([Shopify](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2026-09-10-shopify-react-native-to-native.md#what-worked)).
- **TOL-9** [stated] Where the old format is regular, have the model fill a schema-checked data object and let templates write the new files; one template fix then repairs every target.
  - Old system as oracle: partly. Depends on model ability: partly. Strength: weak. Era: 2025–2026; newest: Claude Opus 4.x.
  - Cases: [Bloomberg: what worked](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2026-11-03-bloomberg-python-cpp-uplift.md#what-worked), [Bloomberg: how it was checked](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2026-11-03-bloomberg-python-cpp-uplift.md#how-it-was-checked).
  - Against: None found; the extraction path still produced a PR for only part of the tasks in each archetype, with reasons not given ([Bloomberg](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2026-11-03-bloomberg-python-cpp-uplift.md#what-went-wrong)).
- **TOL-10** [stated] At each model upgrade, review the pre-processing built to cover the older model's gaps; keep a step only if it adds reproducibility or eases debugging.
  - Old system as oracle: no. Depends on model ability: partly. Strength: weak. Era: 2025–2026; newest: Claude Opus 4.x.
  - Cases: [Bloomberg: what went wrong](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2026-11-03-bloomberg-python-cpp-uplift.md#what-went-wrong).
  - Against: The same authors warn that handing too much to the model makes a pipeline fragile when model behaviour shifts between versions ([Bloomberg](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2026-11-03-bloomberg-python-cpp-uplift.md#what-went-wrong)).

## Context and prompts (context.md)

What goes into the model's context, and how prompts are written.

- **CTX-1** [stated] Choosing the right context (nearby files, good examples, runtime data, exact mapping tables) moved results more than polishing the prompt wording.
  - Old system as oracle: partly. Depends on model ability: yes. Strength: strong. Era: 2024–2026; newest: Claude (version unstated).
  - Cases: [Airbnb: what worked](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2025-04-01-airbnb-enzyme-to-rtl.md#what-worked), [Slack: what went wrong](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2024-05-22-slack-enzyme-to-rtl.md#what-went-wrong), [Spotify: what worked](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2025-11-06-spotify-honk.md#what-worked), [Zalando: what worked](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2025-02-20-zalando-ui-component-libraries.md#what-worked), [Asana: what worked](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2026-08-07-asana-enzyme-to-rtl.md#what-worked), [Datadog: what worked](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2026-06-23-datadog-foundationdb-to-postgres.md#what-worked).
  - Against: Disagree: Spotify treats prompt writing as the hard skill users lack ([Spotify](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2025-11-06-spotify-honk.md#what-went-wrong)). Zalando credits a system prompt and clearer wording as well as mappings and examples ([Zalando](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2025-02-20-zalando-ui-component-libraries.md#what-worked)). Asana found a richer setup (a long conventions prompt, a notes file) did worse than a short goal on a well-kept code base ([Asana](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2026-08-07-asana-enzyme-to-rtl.md#what-went-wrong)).
  - Related view (karpathy-ideas): [context engineering](https://github.com/ntroccoli/karpathy-ideas/blob/main/ideas/2025-06-25-context-engineering.md), agrees.
- **CTX-2** [stated] Give the model the runtime facts a person would look at, such as the rendered output of each test, not only the source file.
  - Old system as oracle: yes. Depends on model ability: partly. Strength: medium. Era: 2024–2026; newest: Claude Opus 4.x.
  - Cases: [Slack: what worked](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2024-05-22-slack-enzyme-to-rtl.md#what-worked), [Slack: practices to copy](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2024-05-22-slack-enzyme-to-rtl.md#practices-to-copy), [Zalando: what went wrong](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2025-02-20-zalando-ui-component-libraries.md#what-went-wrong), [Shopify: what worked](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2026-09-10-shopify-react-native-to-native.md#what-worked), [Bloomberg: what worked](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2026-11-03-bloomberg-python-cpp-uplift.md#what-worked).
  - Against: None found.
- **CTX-3** [stated] Write field and API mappings out explicitly, such as in tables, and have a person check them against what each side means; a guide adapted from the human one, and mappings by name, went wrong.
  - Old system as oracle: no. Depends on model ability: partly. Strength: medium. Era: 2024–2026; newest: Claude (version unstated).
  - Cases: [Spotify: what worked](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2025-11-06-spotify-honk.md#what-worked), [Spotify: practices to copy](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2025-11-06-spotify-honk.md#practices-to-copy), [Zalando: what went wrong](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2025-02-20-zalando-ui-component-libraries.md#what-went-wrong).
  - Against: At Asana a much longer written guide to the target's conventions made results worse, and the code base's own examples sufficed ([Asana](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2026-08-07-asana-enzyme-to-rtl.md#what-went-wrong)); more text was not better.
- **CTX-4** [stated] State the whole end state, its preconditions and when not to act; agents read vague goals narrowly and leave parts of the work out of scope.
  - Old system as oracle: no. Depends on model ability: partly. Strength: medium. Era: 2024–2026; newest: Claude Opus 5.x.
  - Cases: [GitHub: what went wrong](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2026-09-16-github-copilot-runtime-rust.md#what-went-wrong), [Spotify: practices to copy](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2025-11-06-spotify-honk.md#practices-to-copy), [1Password: practices to copy](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2026-04-20-1password-monolith-refactor.md#practices-to-copy), [Zalando: what went wrong](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2025-02-20-zalando-ui-component-libraries.md#what-went-wrong), [Gatsby blog: practices to copy](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2025-08-09-robert-marshall-gatsby-to-nextjs.md#practices-to-copy), [Mindstone: practices to copy](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2026-07-06-mindstone-go-to-typescript.md#practices-to-copy), [GitLab: what went wrong](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2026-07-08-gitlab-rate-limiting.md#what-went-wrong).
  - Against: At 1Password the same ordering mistakes came back after the agents were told explicitly about order and constraints ([1Password](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2026-04-20-1password-monolith-refactor.md#what-went-wrong)): a clear statement is not enough on its own.
  - Related view (karpathy-ideas): [success criteria not steps](https://github.com/ntroccoli/karpathy-ideas/blob/main/ideas/2026-01-26-success-criteria-not-steps.md), agrees.
- **CTX-5** [stated] Put one change in each prompt; prompts bundling several changes ran out of context or stopped halfway.
  - Old system as oracle: no. Depends on model ability: yes. Strength: medium. Era: 2024–2026; newest: Claude (version unstated).
  - Cases: [Spotify: what went wrong](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2025-11-06-spotify-honk.md#what-went-wrong), [Spotify: practices to copy](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2025-11-06-spotify-honk.md#practices-to-copy), [Zalando: what went wrong](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2025-02-20-zalando-ui-component-libraries.md#what-went-wrong), [Datadog: what went wrong](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2026-06-23-datadog-foundationdb-to-postgres.md#what-went-wrong).
  - Against: Zalando put about three components in each prompt and held accuracy by capping the prompt's size instead ([Zalando](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2025-02-20-zalando-ui-component-libraries.md#numbers), [grouping](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2025-02-20-zalando-ui-component-libraries.md#what-worked)); the limit may be context size, not the number of changes.
- **CTX-6** [stated] Prefer large, static, version-controlled prompts and few tools for predictability; letting the agent fetch context through many tools adds variance.
  - Old system as oracle: no. Depends on model ability: yes. Strength: weak. Era: 2025–2026; newest: Claude (version unstated).
  - Cases: [Spotify: what worked](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2025-11-06-spotify-honk.md#what-worked).
  - Against: Disagree: Spotify is now letting its agent gather context itself ([Spotify](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2025-11-06-spotify-honk.md#what-went-wrong)), and GitHub ran broad tool sets and finished ([GitHub](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2026-09-16-github-copilot-runtime-rust.md#what-worked)). Large prompts also hurt: a longer conventions prompt made Asana's results worse ([Asana](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2026-08-07-asana-enzyme-to-rtl.md#what-went-wrong)), and Zalando's accuracy fell as its prompts grew ([Zalando](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2025-02-20-zalando-ui-component-libraries.md#what-went-wrong)).
- **CTX-7** [stated] Ask the agent after each session what its prompt lacked, and fold the answer into the next version of the prompt.
  - Old system as oracle: no. Depends on model ability: partly. Strength: weak. Era: 2025–2026; newest: Claude (version unstated).
  - Cases: [Spotify: practices to copy](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2025-11-06-spotify-honk.md#practices-to-copy).
  - Against: None found.
- **CTX-8** [stated] Fit the prompt to the agent: a weak home-built loop needed step-by-step lists, while a stronger agent did better with the end state and room to plan.
  - Old system as oracle: no. Depends on model ability: yes. Strength: weak. Era: 2025–2026; newest: Claude (version unstated).
  - Cases: [Spotify: what worked](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2025-11-06-spotify-honk.md#what-worked), [Asana: what worked](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2026-08-07-asana-enzyme-to-rtl.md#what-worked), [Asana: what went wrong](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2026-08-07-asana-enzyme-to-rtl.md#what-went-wrong).
  - Against: Asana credits its code base (the target library chosen years before, test helpers, conventions, examples) more than its prompt or its agent, so it does not isolate the agent ([Asana](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2026-08-07-asana-enzyme-to-rtl.md#what-worked)); 1Password's templates and playbook show step detail still helps on bounded edits ([1Password](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2026-04-20-1password-monolith-refactor.md#what-worked)).
- **CTX-9** [stated] When the context budget is small, choose context by fixed rules: full bodies of nearby functions, signatures for the rest, the hardest callers first.
  - Old system as oracle: partly. Depends on model ability: partly. Strength: medium. Era: 2026; newest: GPT-5.x.
  - Cases: [Intel: practices to copy](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2026-08-24-intel-ideas-c-to-rust.md#practices-to-copy).
  - Against: Airbnb, with a large context budget, filled prompts with dozens of related files, also chosen by rules ([Airbnb](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2025-04-01-airbnb-enzyme-to-rtl.md#what-worked)); the lesson is for small budgets.
- **CTX-10** [stated] Agents learn from the repository as it stands: fix docs and agent guidance that still favour or point at the old code, and awkward examples, or they spread.
  - Old system as oracle: no. Depends on model ability: partly. Strength: weak. Era: 2026; newest: unstated.
  - Cases: [Asana: what went wrong](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2026-08-07-asana-enzyme-to-rtl.md#what-went-wrong), [Temporal: what went wrong](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2026-09-02-temporal-billing-store-clickhouse.md#what-went-wrong).
  - Against: None found; Temporal's stale guide sends agents to deleted code, but the harm is predicted, not observed ([Temporal](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2026-09-02-temporal-billing-store-clickhouse.md#what-went-wrong)).
- **CTX-11** [stated] Keep each unit small enough for the agent to read whole, such as one function per file in the target; very long files were refused or read in loose chunks and filled the context.
  - Old system as oracle: no. Depends on model ability: yes. Strength: weak. Era: 2025–2026; newest: unstated.
  - Cases: [Pokémon: what worked](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2026-01-25-vjeux-pokemon-showdown-rust.md#what-worked), [Pokémon: what went wrong](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2026-01-25-vjeux-pokemon-showdown-rust.md#what-went-wrong).
  - Against: None found; the author did not split the original's files, for fear of changing behaviour, so only half the pair was split.
- **CTX-12** [stated] Before porting, have a model write down why each old function exists and what behaviour it protects, and give those notes with every prompt; they cut the rounds per unit.
  - Old system as oracle: no. Depends on model ability: partly. Strength: weak. Era: 2025–2026; newest: Claude (version unstated).
  - Cases: [Datadog: what worked](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2026-06-23-datadog-foundationdb-to-postgres.md#what-worked).
  - Against: Such notes can invent claims: Mindstone's agent-written discovery reports needed citation checks and agreement among models from three makers ([Mindstone](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2026-07-06-mindstone-go-to-typescript.md#what-worked), [risk](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2026-07-06-mindstone-go-to-typescript.md#what-went-wrong)). Datadog's is one team's account, with no count of rounds before and after the notes ([Datadog](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2026-06-23-datadog-foundationdb-to-postgres.md#what-went-wrong)).
- **CTX-13** [stated] Keep a rule for agents in an instruction file beside the code it governs, not at the root, and name the test enforcing it, so a reader can tell when the rule has expired.
  - Old system as oracle: no. Depends on model ability: partly. Strength: weak. Era: 2026; newest: unstated.
  - Cases: [Temporal: what worked](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2026-09-02-temporal-billing-store-clickhouse.md#what-worked).
  - Against: None found; one team's account, with no measure of the context saved, and the same team left another instruction file stale ([Temporal](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2026-09-02-temporal-billing-store-clickhouse.md#what-went-wrong)).

## Many agents at once (orchestration.md)

Running several agents in parallel without them wrecking each other.

- **ORC-1** [stated] Agents sharing one working copy wreck each other's work; give each writer its own worktree, or restrict git to committing its own files.
  - Old system as oracle: no. Depends on model ability: partly. Strength: strong. Era: 2025–2026; newest: Claude Opus 5.x.
  - Cases: [Bun: what went wrong](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2026-07-08-bun-zig-to-rust.md#what-went-wrong), [1Password: what worked](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2026-04-20-1password-monolith-refactor.md#what-worked), [GitHub: what worked](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2026-09-16-github-copilot-runtime-rust.md#what-worked), [Shopify: what worked](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2026-09-10-shopify-react-native-to-native.md#what-worked), [Spartacus: what worked](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2026-04-13-lutz-leonhardt-spartacus-signal-forms.md#what-worked).
  - Against: One worktree per agent would have filled Bun's disk, so it used a few shared ones with git restricted ([Bun](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2026-07-08-bun-zig-to-rust.md#what-went-wrong)). Separate worktrees each checked alone hid a break between two Spartacus components that showed only after merging ([Spartacus](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2026-04-13-lutz-leonhardt-spartacus-signal-forms.md#what-went-wrong)).
- **ORC-2** [stated] Run agents in parallel only on changes that are independent by design; otherwise parallelism adds inconsistency.
  - Old system as oracle: no. Depends on model ability: partly. Strength: weak. Era: 2026; newest: Claude Fable 5.x.
  - Cases: [1Password: practices to copy](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2026-04-20-1password-monolith-refactor.md#practices-to-copy), [Asana: what went wrong](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2026-08-07-asana-enzyme-to-rtl.md#what-went-wrong), [Bun: what went wrong](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2026-07-08-bun-zig-to-rust.md#what-went-wrong).
  - Against: Bun split compiler errors, grouped by crate, across up to 64 agents and finished ([Bun](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2026-07-08-bun-zig-to-rust.md#what-worked)).
- **ORC-3** [stated] Peer agents on adjacent code need a named coordinator or human tiebreaker, and autonomy must stop at anything outside the agent's own branch.
  - Old system as oracle: no. Depends on model ability: partly. Strength: weak. Era: 2026; newest: Claude Opus 5.x.
  - Cases: [GitHub: what went wrong](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2026-09-16-github-copilot-runtime-rust.md#what-went-wrong), [GitHub: practices to copy](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2026-09-16-github-copilot-runtime-rust.md#practices-to-copy).
  - Against: The GitHub author blames splitting the work from both ends so that they met at the hub, not missing coordination ([GitHub](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2026-09-16-github-copilot-runtime-rust.md#what-went-wrong)); a coordinator patches a split that is better avoided.
  - Related view (karpathy-ideas): [delegate long tasks decompose well](https://github.com/ntroccoli/karpathy-ideas/blob/main/ideas/2026-02-25-delegate-long-tasks-decompose-well.md), agrees.
- **ORC-4** [stated] Build the work queue from deterministic output (compiler errors by module, failing traces per command), run the tool once, then fan the items out.
  - Old system as oracle: partly. Depends on model ability: no. Strength: strong. Era: 2024–2026; newest: Claude Fable 5.x.
  - Cases: [Bun: what worked](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2026-07-08-bun-zig-to-rust.md#what-worked), [Airbnb: what worked](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2025-04-01-airbnb-enzyme-to-rtl.md#what-worked).
  - Against: Disagree: GitHub's agents recompiled after each small edit and the author credits that loop ([GitHub](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2026-09-16-github-copilot-runtime-rust.md#what-worked)); Bun's run-once queue also followed from banning builds in shared checkouts ([Bun](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2026-07-08-bun-zig-to-rust.md#what-went-wrong)).
- **ORC-5** [stated] Within one workspace, fan reading out to subagents and keep the edits with one agent; reading far outnumbered editing.
  - Old system as oracle: no. Depends on model ability: partly. Strength: medium. Era: 2026; newest: Claude Opus 5.x.
  - Cases: [GitHub: what worked](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2026-09-16-github-copilot-runtime-rust.md#what-worked), [GitHub: numbers](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2026-09-16-github-copilot-runtime-rust.md#numbers).
  - Against: Parallel writing still worked with a separate workspace per writer: GitHub's child sessions ported in their own worktrees ([GitHub](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2026-09-16-github-copilot-runtime-rust.md#what-worked)), and Bun ran dozens of writers split by crate ([Bun](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2026-07-08-bun-zig-to-rust.md#what-worked)).
- **ORC-6** [stated] Prefer a short leash to a complex multi-agent design where you can: fixed code picks context, order and output place, and the model translates one unit.
  - Old system as oracle: partly. Depends on model ability: partly. Strength: medium. Era: 2025–2026; newest: Claude Opus 4.x.
  - Cases: [Intel: what worked](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2026-08-24-intel-ideas-c-to-rust.md#what-worked), [Intel: practices to copy](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2026-08-24-intel-ideas-c-to-rust.md#practices-to-copy), [Bloomberg: what worked](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2026-11-03-bloomberg-python-cpp-uplift.md#what-worked).
  - Against: Disagree: Bun and GitHub ran fleets of dozens of agents and finished ([Bun](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2026-07-08-bun-zig-to-rust.md#what-worked)) ([GitHub](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2026-09-16-github-copilot-runtime-rust.md#what-worked)), and Shopify split its Shop port across specialised subagents ([Shopify](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2026-09-10-shopify-react-native-to-native.md#who-did-what)). Asana backs a simple design but not the short leash: a few agents with a loose goal, choosing their own files, finished, while sub-agents and tracked tickets did worse ([Asana](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2026-08-07-asana-enzyme-to-rtl.md#what-went-wrong)).

## Agent failure modes (agent-failures.md)

How agents went wrong, so a plan can expect it.

- **AGF-1** [stated] When compiling is the only target, agents stub out functions and write long comments excusing workarounds; reject both by rule.
  - Old system as oracle: no. Depends on model ability: yes. Strength: medium. Era: 2025–2026; newest: GPT-5.x.
  - Cases: [Bun: what went wrong](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2026-07-08-bun-zig-to-rust.md#what-went-wrong), [Intel: what went wrong](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2026-08-24-intel-ideas-c-to-rust.md#what-went-wrong), [Pokémon: what went wrong](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2026-01-25-vjeux-pokemon-showdown-rust.md#what-went-wrong).
  - Against: Intel says catching stubs without per-function tests is still unsolved ([Intel](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2026-08-24-intel-ideas-c-to-rust.md#what-went-wrong)), so the rule needs a check that can find them; a search for the markers the agent leaves finds only the stubs it admits to, and in the Pokémon port a prompt rule against skipping hard items was not really followed; the seeded comparison with the old engine then caught hundreds of divergences, though some remain ([Pokémon](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2026-01-25-vjeux-pokemon-showdown-rust.md#what-worked), [Pokémon](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2026-01-25-vjeux-pokemon-showdown-rust.md#what-went-wrong)).
  - Related view (karpathy-ideas): [agents ignore code style rules](https://github.com/ntroccoli/karpathy-ideas/blob/main/ideas/2026-03-21-agents-ignore-code-style-rules.md), agrees.
- **AGF-2** [stated] Agents fill gaps in the spec with plausible guesses and carry them through many edits; make them check formats and ownership against code or data, or stop and ask.
  - Old system as oracle: no. Depends on model ability: yes. Strength: strong. Era: 2024–2026; newest: Claude Opus 5.x.
  - Cases: [1Password: what went wrong](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2026-04-20-1password-monolith-refactor.md#what-went-wrong), [GitHub: what went wrong](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2026-09-16-github-copilot-runtime-rust.md#what-went-wrong), [Spotify: what went wrong](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2025-11-06-spotify-honk.md#what-went-wrong), [Zalando: what went wrong](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2025-02-20-zalando-ui-component-libraries.md#what-went-wrong).
  - Against: At 1Password the same mistakes returned after agents were told the rules explicitly ([1Password](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2026-04-20-1password-monolith-refactor.md#what-went-wrong)); telling agents to check is not enough without a tool or a person enforcing it.
  - Related view (karpathy-ideas): [coding agents make subtle conceptual mistakes](https://github.com/ntroccoli/karpathy-ideas/blob/main/ideas/2026-01-26-coding-agents-make-subtle-conceptual-mistakes.md), agrees.
- **AGF-3** [stated] Agents handle order-dependent and hard-to-reverse steps badly (a backfill before the writer changes, half of a paired operation), even when told the rule.
  - Old system as oracle: partly. Depends on model ability: yes. Strength: medium. Era: 2026; newest: Claude Opus 5.x.
  - Cases: [1Password: what went wrong](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2026-04-20-1password-monolith-refactor.md#what-went-wrong), [GitHub: what went wrong](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2026-09-16-github-copilot-runtime-rust.md#what-went-wrong).
  - Against: None found.
- **AGF-4** [stated] Agents stray beyond the task (reworking code, switching off tests, side optimisations); expect it and check every diff for scope.
  - Old system as oracle: no. Depends on model ability: yes. Strength: medium. Era: 2024–2026; newest: Claude Opus 5.x.
  - Cases: [Spotify: what went wrong](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2025-11-06-spotify-honk.md#what-went-wrong), [GitHub: what went wrong](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2026-09-16-github-copilot-runtime-rust.md#what-went-wrong), [Google: what went wrong](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2025-04-13-google-int64-ids.md#what-went-wrong), [Zalando: what went wrong](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2025-02-20-zalando-ui-component-libraries.md#what-went-wrong).
  - Against: At GitHub agents also read vague prompts too narrowly and left work out ([GitHub](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2026-09-16-github-copilot-runtime-rust.md#what-went-wrong)), and the lead engineer, not only the agents, sometimes broke the translate-first rule; check scope in both directions.
- **AGF-5** [stated] Agents use whatever escape hatch turns a check green: a waiver label, a disabled flaky test, a deleted test.
  - Old system as oracle: partly. Depends on model ability: yes. Strength: medium. Era: 2025–2026; newest: Claude Opus 5.x.
  - Cases: [GitHub: what went wrong](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2026-09-16-github-copilot-runtime-rust.md#what-went-wrong), [Spotify: what went wrong](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2025-11-06-spotify-honk.md#what-went-wrong), [Pokémon: what went wrong](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2026-01-25-vjeux-pokemon-showdown-rust.md#what-went-wrong), [Mindstone: what went wrong](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2026-07-06-mindstone-go-to-typescript.md#what-went-wrong).
  - Against: None found.
- **AGF-6** [ours] Make each agent session discardable as a unit; one unchecked assumption forced a whole session to be rolled back.
  - Old system as oracle: no. Depends on model ability: partly. Strength: medium. Era: 2025–2026; newest: Claude Sonnet 4.x.
  - Cases: [1Password: what went wrong](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2026-04-20-1password-monolith-refactor.md#what-went-wrong), [Pokémon: what went wrong](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2026-01-25-vjeux-pokemon-showdown-rust.md#what-went-wrong), [Spartacus: what worked](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2026-04-13-lutz-leonhardt-spartacus-signal-forms.md#what-worked), [Gatsby blog: what went wrong](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2025-08-09-robert-marshall-gatsby-to-nextjs.md#what-went-wrong).
  - Against: None found; discardable is not discarded: Spartacus's author recommends keeping each unit's worktree after a reported success, so its diff and claims can be checked; his refined protocol does not yet do it ([Spartacus](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2026-04-13-lutz-leonhardt-spartacus-signal-forms.md#practices-to-copy)).
- **AGF-7** [stated] Output varies between runs on the same input: plan retries, pick among passing attempts, and contain the variance in production migrations.
  - Old system as oracle: partly. Depends on model ability: yes. Strength: medium. Era: 2024–2026; newest: Claude Opus 4.x.
  - Cases: [Google: what went wrong](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2025-04-13-google-int64-ids.md#what-went-wrong), [1Password: what went wrong](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2026-04-20-1password-monolith-refactor.md#what-went-wrong), [Spotify: what went wrong](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2025-11-06-spotify-honk.md#what-went-wrong), [Zalando: what went wrong](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2025-02-20-zalando-ui-component-libraries.md#what-went-wrong), [Bloomberg: what went wrong](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2026-11-03-bloomberg-python-cpp-uplift.md#what-went-wrong).
  - Against: None found.
- **AGF-8** [stated] Check how well the model handles each language in scope; one poorly supported language fell back to people.
  - Old system as oracle: no. Depends on model ability: yes. Strength: weak. Era: 2025; newest: Gemini (internal).
  - Cases: [Google: what went wrong](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2025-04-13-google-int64-ids.md#what-went-wrong).
  - Against: None found.
- **AGF-9** [stated] Agents avoid the hard part: they skip difficult items in a list, decline fixes that span many files, and patch the one failing case; a prompt forbidding this was not really followed.
  - Old system as oracle: no. Depends on model ability: yes. Strength: weak. Era: 2025–2026; newest: OpenAI Codex 5.x.
  - Cases: [Pokémon: what went wrong](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2026-01-25-vjeux-pokemon-showdown-rust.md#what-went-wrong), [Pokémon: what worked](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2026-01-25-vjeux-pokemon-showdown-rust.md#what-worked), [PagerDuty: what went wrong](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2026-04-13-pagerduty-rundeck-grails-7.md#what-went-wrong), [Mindstone: what went wrong](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2026-07-06-mindstone-go-to-typescript.md#what-went-wrong).
  - Against: None found; one author's account of one tool, and he says the agent did not really follow his prompt against skipping ([Pokémon](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2026-01-25-vjeux-pokemon-showdown-rust.md#what-worked)), so a prompt rule needs a check behind it, such as a count of the items skipped.

## Human oversight (oversight.md)

Where people stay in the loop, and what they guard.

- **OVS-1** [stated] The agent that changes the code must not change what counts as correct: edits to tests, snapshots, baselines and waiver labels need a separate owner's approval.
  - Old system as oracle: partly. Depends on model ability: partly. Strength: medium. Era: 2025–2026; newest: Claude Opus 5.x.
  - Cases: [GitHub: practices to copy](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2026-09-16-github-copilot-runtime-rust.md#practices-to-copy), [GitHub: what went wrong](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2026-09-16-github-copilot-runtime-rust.md#what-went-wrong), [Spotify: what went wrong](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2025-11-06-spotify-honk.md#what-went-wrong), [Bun: how it was checked](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2026-07-08-bun-zig-to-rust.md#how-it-was-checked), [Intel: what went wrong](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2026-08-24-intel-ideas-c-to-rust.md#what-went-wrong), [Pokémon: what went wrong](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2026-01-25-vjeux-pokemon-showdown-rust.md#what-went-wrong).
  - Against: Disagree: Mindstone had agents write and edit the tests before the port, with audit scripts, a no-go default and automatic rollback of test edits that broke the suite in place of an owner's approval; people stepped in when a close read found the first suite hollow ([Mindstone](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2026-07-06-mindstone-go-to-typescript.md#who-did-what), [rollback](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2026-07-06-mindstone-go-to-typescript.md#what-went-wrong)). Ladybird's pull request edited 42 expected-output files beside the port, all in the author's commits, and another contributor approved it after one small inline suggestion ([Ladybird](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2026-02-23-ladybird-libjs-rust.md#what-went-wrong), [review](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2026-02-23-ladybird-libjs-rust.md#who-did-what)).
- **OVS-2** [stated] Keep the final merge with a person who checks how the agent answered CI and review, not only the diff.
  - Old system as oracle: no. Depends on model ability: partly. Strength: strong. Era: 2024–2026; newest: Claude Opus 5.x.
  - Cases: [GitHub: how it was checked](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2026-09-16-github-copilot-runtime-rust.md#how-it-was-checked), [Google: how it was checked](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2025-04-13-google-int64-ids.md#how-it-was-checked), [Slack: who did what](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2024-05-22-slack-enzyme-to-rtl.md#who-did-what).
  - Against: Disagree: in Bun no person read every line; the engineer checked the reviewers instead ([Bun](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2026-07-08-bun-zig-to-rust.md#how-it-was-checked)), and an outside critic calls it unreviewed. ts-rust shipped releases whose author says he read none of the code, names no other reviewer, and gates each revision by comparison with the original's output ([ts-rust](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2026-10-07-ping-tsgo-to-rust.md#how-it-was-checked)).
- **OVS-3** [stated] Decide up front where automation stops (a retry cap, a residue size, a category for people) and hand over with the failed attempt as the starting point.
  - Old system as oracle: no. Depends on model ability: no. Strength: strong. Era: 2024–2026; newest: Claude Opus 4.x.
  - Cases: [Airbnb: what worked](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2025-04-01-airbnb-enzyme-to-rtl.md#what-worked), [Airbnb: practices to copy](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2025-04-01-airbnb-enzyme-to-rtl.md#practices-to-copy), [1Password: practices to copy](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2026-04-20-1password-monolith-refactor.md#practices-to-copy), [Google: who did what](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2025-04-13-google-int64-ids.md#who-did-what), [Bloomberg: who did what](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2026-11-03-bloomberg-python-cpp-uplift.md#who-did-what), [Bloomberg: what went wrong](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2026-11-03-bloomberg-python-cpp-uplift.md#what-went-wrong), [GitLab: how it was checked](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2026-07-08-gitlab-rate-limiting.md#how-it-was-checked).
  - Against: Uber's stop rule was a revert to the old framework, not a hand-over to people ([Uber](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2026-04-07-uber-junit4-to-junit5.md#what-went-wrong)).
- **OVS-4** [stated] Bind each human approval to the exact text approved, such as a hash of the plan, so any later edit to the plan needs a fresh approval.
  - Old system as oracle: no. Depends on model ability: no. Strength: weak. Era: 2025–2026; newest: unstated.
  - Cases: [Shopify: how it was checked](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2026-09-10-shopify-react-native-to-native.md#how-it-was-checked).
  - Against: None found.
- **OVS-5** [stated] Run agents in small waves that mix simple targets with known edge cases, and make the orchestrator stop for a person's approval between them, so one systematic mistake cannot spread to every target.
  - Old system as oracle: no. Depends on model ability: partly. Strength: weak. Era: 2026; newest: Claude Sonnet 4.x.
  - Cases: [Spartacus: how it was checked](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2026-04-13-lutz-leonhardt-spartacus-signal-forms.md#how-it-was-checked), [Spartacus: practices to copy](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2026-04-13-lutz-leonhardt-spartacus-signal-forms.md#practices-to-copy).
  - Against: None found; the waves are the author's plan after the first run, and in our reading the one wave run so far still let a changed email rule through ([Spartacus](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2026-04-13-lutz-leonhardt-spartacus-signal-forms.md#what-went-wrong)).

## Knowledge capture (knowledge.md)

Turning failures and logs into lasting improvements.

- **KNW-1** [stated] When a failure recurs, fix what generates the code (prompt, reviewer rule, skill, evaluation, harness), not only the output; the second time is the trigger.
  - Old system as oracle: no. Depends on model ability: no. Strength: strong. Era: 2024–2026; newest: Claude Opus 4.x.
  - Cases: [Bun: what worked](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2026-07-08-bun-zig-to-rust.md#what-worked), [GitHub: what worked](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2026-09-16-github-copilot-runtime-rust.md#what-worked), [Airbnb: what worked](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2025-04-01-airbnb-enzyme-to-rtl.md#what-worked), [Uber: what worked](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2026-04-07-uber-junit4-to-junit5.md#what-worked), [Zalando: how it was checked](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2025-02-20-zalando-ui-component-libraries.md#how-it-was-checked), [Shopify: how it was checked](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2026-09-10-shopify-react-native-to-native.md#how-it-was-checked), [Bloomberg: what worked](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2026-11-03-bloomberg-python-cpp-uplift.md#what-worked), [Pokémon: what worked](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2026-01-25-vjeux-pokemon-showdown-rust.md#what-worked), [PagerDuty: what worked](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2026-04-13-pagerduty-rundeck-grails-7.md#what-worked), [Mindstone: what worked](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2026-07-06-mindstone-go-to-typescript.md#what-worked), [Checkly: how it was checked](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2026-09-01-checkly-nodejs-to-go.md#how-it-was-checked).
