- A written list of look-alike constructs helps reviewers and agents, and takes a person who knows
  both stacks to write (REV-3).
- Testing every shipped platform catches runtime defaults and multiplies the test matrix (OPS-4).

### When not to apply it

- A pitfalls item marked "(ours)" has no case behind it: search for it, and weigh what you find as
  the maintainer's inference (ours).
- A move within one runtime (a library upgrade) keeps most runtime defaults; the release notes
  between the two versions are the better list there (ours).

## Q8 guide: Is the code uniform enough for one prompt, and what context goes with it?

For question 8 of the [checklist](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/checklist.md): read it before writing up a finding on that
question. It walks through what the cases show; the project's owner decides. Each point names its
evidence: a lesson ID (its strength, its cases and the cases against it are in
[lessons/evidence.md](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/lessons/evidence.md); its page links the case sections) or a case link.
"(ours)" marks the maintainer's reading, evidence level `ours`; so does a lesson tagged `[ours]` there,
which is our inference from its cases.

### Lessons behind it

- [CTX-1](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/lessons/context.md): the right context moved results more than prompt wording.
- [CTX-2](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/lessons/context.md): runtime facts a person would look at, such as a test's rendered
  output.
- [CTX-3](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/lessons/context.md): field and API mappings written out and checked by a person.
- [CTX-5](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/lessons/context.md): one change per prompt.
- [CTX-9](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/lessons/context.md): with a small context budget, context chosen by fixed rules.
- [CTX-10](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/lessons/context.md): docs and agent guidance that favour the old code steer agents
  back to it.
- [CTX-11](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/lessons/context.md): units small enough to read whole.
- [CTX-12](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/lessons/context.md), [CTX-13](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/lessons/context.md): notes on why old code exists;
  rules kept beside the code they govern.
- [TOL-2](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/lessons/tooling.md), [TOL-7](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/lessons/tooling.md), [TOL-9](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/lessons/tooling.md): a
  rule-based codemod or template first, the model after.
- [AGF-8](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/lessons/agent-failures.md): one poorly supported language fell back to people.
- [PLN-8](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/lessons/planning.md), [PLN-12](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/lessons/planning.md): segments that cannot be
  specified left out; archetypes each with its own prompt.

Cases, in our words: Spotify dropped a framework too varied for one prompt; mapping tables fixed
wrong field mappings. Airbnb's choice of related files mattered more than wording; Slack gave the
model a codemod's partial output and each test's rendered output. Google's model handled Dart
poorly, so people did it; Uber's recipes did a move its AI attempt failed. Bloomberg gave each
kind of target its own prompt; stale docs misled Asana's agents; Pokémon split files the agent
would not open.

### What it looks like in a project

- Several kinds of code in scope (pure logic, concurrency, OS layer, UI, data pipelines), each
  needing its own prompt and examples (PLN-12).
- Renamed fields or APIs with no written mapping, which a model maps by name and gets wrong
  ([Zalando](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2025-02-20-zalando-ui-component-libraries.md#what-went-wrong), CTX-3).
- Files too long for the model to read whole ([Pokémon](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2026-01-25-vjeux-pokemon-showdown-rust.md#what-went-wrong)).
- Docs or agent instructions that still recommend the old library ([Asana](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2026-08-07-asana-enzyme-to-rtl.md#what-went-wrong)).

### Questions to ask of this project

- Into which groups does the code fall, by kind, framework, build system and style?
- For each group, what context would an agent get: source, neighbours' tests, examples, mappings,
  runtime facts?
- What can a rule-based codemod do first?
- How does the model do on the hardest files of each language in scope?
- Which docs or instructions still point at the old stack?

### Trade-offs

- A codemod first anchors the model and costs rules that grow on long-tail patterns (TOL-2,
  TOL-4).
- A prompt per group gives better results and more prompts to maintain (PLN-12).
- Deferring a varied group or doing it by hand keeps the pipeline simple and leaves part of the
  move undone (PLN-8).

### When not to apply it

- Lessons about what models handle well or badly age fast: see whether
  [lessons/index.md](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/lessons/index.md) marks AGF-8 or TOL-2 "may be outdated", and pilot on the
  model you will use (AGF-8).
- A small, uniform scope needs no grouping; the context list still applies (ours).

## Q9 guide: How will you work the long tail, stop, and learn from failures?

For question 9 of the [checklist](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/checklist.md): read it before writing up a finding on that
question. It walks through what the cases show; the project's owner decides. Each point names its
evidence: a lesson ID (its strength, its cases and the cases against it are in
[lessons/evidence.md](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/lessons/evidence.md); its page links the case sections) or a case link.
"(ours)" marks the maintainer's reading, evidence level `ours`; so does a lesson tagged `[ours]` there,
which is our inference from its cases.

### Lessons behind it

- [VER-3](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/lessons/verification.md): a failed unit retried with its latest errors in a fresh
  prompt, a bounded number of times, then handed to people; it fits independent units.
- [KNW-1](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/lessons/knowledge.md): when a failure recurs, what generates the code is fixed, not
  only the output; the second time is the trigger.
- [KNW-2](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/lessons/knowledge.md): each unit stamped with its status, the largest failing group
  tuned on a sample, then everything swept again.
- [KNW-4](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/lessons/knowledge.md), [KNW-5](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/lessons/knowledge.md): the method kept in files a
  fresh session rereads; temporary migration code marked when written.
- [OVS-3](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/lessons/oversight.md): where automation hands over to people decided up front.
- [OVS-5](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/lessons/oversight.md): small waves with a person's approval between them.
- [CTX-7](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/lessons/context.md): the agent asked after each session what its prompt lacked.
- [AGF-7](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/lessons/agent-failures.md): output varies between runs on the same input.
- [OPS-6](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/lessons/operations.md): bulk jobs in scheduled batches, results sorted by status,
  only the stuck ones rerun.
- [ROL-8](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/lessons/rollout.md): a unit that fails its tests sent back to the old framework.
- [TST-11](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/lessons/testing.md): a golden set rerun after each prompt change.

Cases, in our words: Airbnb stamped each file with its status, swept again after each fix and
finished the last files by hand; Intel capped retries. GitHub turned repeated failures into
instructions, skills and evals; Spotify asks the agent what its prompt lacked; Zalando reran a
golden set after each prompt change. Uber put files whose tests failed back on the old framework.
ts-rust's first attempt stalled for months, no stop rule stated; Spartacus now stops for a person
after each wave.

### What it looks like in a project

- A plan that retries every failing unit until it passes, with no bound and no hand-over
  ([Airbnb](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2025-04-01-airbnb-enzyme-to-rtl.md#what-worked), [ts-rust](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2026-10-07-ping-tsgo-to-rust.md#what-went-wrong)).
- Units that depend on each other, where a failure downstream often comes from a wrong unit
  upstream (VER-3's "Against").
- The same failure fixed by hand in many outputs, with no change to the prompt or tool that made it
  (KNW-1).
- No status per unit, so a rerun redoes what already passed (KNW-2).

### Questions to ask of this project

- Which units are independent, and which depend on others?
- Where is each unit's status kept, and can a failing unit be rerun from the step that failed?
- After how many attempts, or what signal, does a unit go to a person?
- Where does a failure seen twice become an instruction, a skill or an eval?
- What is the rule for stopping the automation as a whole?

### Trade-offs

- A bound on retries saves attempts on units that will not pass and sends some units to people
  that one more try would have fixed (VER-3; rows P6 and P9 of the checklist's Provenance table).
- Fixing the prompt or tool after a repeated failure costs a rerun of everything it made, and
  saves fixing each output by hand (KNW-1).
- Waves with a person's approval between them contain a systematic mistake and slow the run
  (OVS-5).

### When not to apply it

- A count of attempts suits small independent units such as files; for units in a chain, fixing
  the workflow and rerunning from the first wrong unit fits better (VER-3, row P6).
- Airbnb's numbers come from test files of simple and medium difficulty; they say nothing about
  packages or services (VER-3; row P9 of the checklist's Provenance table).

## Q10 guide: What may the agent decide and reach alone, and who reviews?

For question 10 of the [checklist](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/checklist.md): read it before writing up a finding on that
question. It walks through what the cases show; the project's owner decides. Each point names its
evidence: a lesson ID (its strength, its cases and the cases against it are in
[lessons/evidence.md](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/lessons/evidence.md); its page links the case sections) or a case link.
"(ours)" marks the maintainer's reading, evidence level `ours`; so does a lesson tagged `[ours]` there,
which is our inference from its cases.

### Lessons behind it

- [OVS-1](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/lessons/oversight.md): edits to tests, snapshots, baselines and waiver labels need an
  owner's approval separate from the agent.
- [OVS-2](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/lessons/oversight.md): the final merge kept with a person who checks how the agent
  answered CI and review.
- [AGF-1](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/lessons/agent-failures.md), [AGF-5](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/lessons/agent-failures.md),
  [AGF-9](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/lessons/agent-failures.md): agents stubbed functions, used escape hatches and avoided
  the hard part.
- [SEC-1](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/lessons/security.md), [SEC-2](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/lessons/security.md),
  [SEC-3](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/lessons/security.md): a minimal sandbox; whatever the harness exposes may get used;
  destructive commands blocked in the tool layer.
- [REV-1](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/lessons/review.md), [REV-2](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/lessons/review.md): reviewers in fresh contexts other
  than the writer; people on architecture and flagged risk.
- [REV-9](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/lessons/review.md), [REV-11](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/lessons/review.md): review by the owning teams became
  the bottleneck; reviewers who know the target platform.
- [TEM-4](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/lessons/team.md), [TEM-6](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/lessons/team.md): review in two tiers; the people doing
  it get drained.
- [ROL-9](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/lessons/rollout.md): unrequested changes mostly sat undecided.

Cases, in our words: a GitHub agent applied a waiver label to pass a failing check, and a session
merged a peer's worktree unasked; Spotify's agents switched off unreliable tests; Bun's agents
stubbed functions until reviewer agents, seeing only the diff, rejected that; 1Password's agents
repeated ordering mistakes after being told. Most of Bloomberg's unrequested pull requests got no
decision from their owners; Shopify needed reviewers who knew the target platform.

### What it looks like in a project

- Guardrails an agent can switch off: a waiver label, a flag that skips a check, write access to
  snapshots ([GitHub](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2026-09-16-github-copilot-runtime-rust.md#what-went-wrong), AGF-5).
- A rule written in agent instructions with nothing in CI or the tool layer enforcing it (SEC-3).
- Changes landing in other teams' code that did not ask for the move ([Bloomberg](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2026-11-03-bloomberg-python-cpp-uplift.md#what-went-wrong)).
- One reviewer, who does not read the target language, with a few hours a week (REV-9, REV-11).

### Questions to ask of this project

- Which guardrails could an agent switch off, and who must approve each?
- Which steps stay with people (schema changes, backfills, deploy order)?
- Which tools, skills and credentials can agent sessions reach?
- Which written rules does nothing enforce?
- Who reviews, do they read the target language, and how many hours a week do they have?

### Trade-offs

- Enforcing a rule in CI or the tool layer holds where an instruction did not, and costs setup and
  some false blocks (SEC-3).
- Reviewer agents in fresh contexts catch stubs and drift cheaply; their miss rate is unmeasured,
  so keeping the merge with a person is one option (REV-1, REV-5, OVS-2).
- Sending changes to other teams spreads the review load and leaves many changes undecided
  (ROL-9, TEM-4).

### When not to apply it

- A solo project where the owner is the only reviewer has no team to spread the load to; the
  hours a week still bound how fast agents' changes can land (ours).
- A sandboxed agent with no credentials needs fewer guardrails on what it can reach, not on what
  counts as correct (SEC-1, OVS-1).

## Q11 guide: How will changes reach users?

For question 11 of the [checklist](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/checklist.md): read it before writing up a finding on that
question. It walks through what the cases show; the project's owner decides. Each point names its
evidence: a lesson ID (its strength, its cases and the cases against it are in
[lessons/evidence.md](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/lessons/evidence.md); its page links the case sections) or a case link.
"(ours)" marks the maintainer's reading, evidence level `ours`; so does a lesson tagged `[ours]` there,
which is our inference from its cases.

### Lessons behind it

- [ROL-2](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/lessons/rollout.md): merged and released as separate gates; a canary or pre-release
  first.
- [ROL-3](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/lessons/rollout.md): slow production rollouts watched by owners; the pipeline speeds
  the code, not this step.
- [ROL-5](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/lessons/rollout.md): short-lived agent branches against a busy main branch.
- [ROL-7](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/lessons/rollout.md): a new failure boundary shipped as an opt-in mode beside the old
  default.
- [ROL-10](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/lessons/rollout.md): shadow comparison aimed at the largest and oddest inputs, with
  mismatches labelled.
- [ROL-11](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/lessons/rollout.md): cut over in order of how costly a mistake is to undo,
  read-only paths first.
- [VER-1](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/lessons/verification.md): a green build shows the parts fit, not that behaviour
  survived.
- [OPS-5](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/lessons/operations.md), [OPS-8](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/lessons/operations.md): hardening after merge;
  headroom of shared services under double load.

Cases, in our words: GitHub aimed to ship each port to a pre-release first, yet some regressions
reached stable; Bun's merged build stayed a canary while regressions were fixed; Google rolled its
largest migrations out slowly, owners watching. Temporal compared every query and cut over
read-only paths first; GitLab ramped to full traffic past a divergence its shadow run flagged but
did not label. A rollback path per unit is ours.

### What it looks like in a project

- Release channels (pre-release, flags, canary) and the share of users each reaches
  ([GitHub](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2026-09-16-github-copilot-runtime-rust.md#what-went-wrong), ROL-2).
- A shadow run whose mismatches are counted but not labelled by kind ([GitLab](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2026-07-08-gitlab-rate-limiting.md#what-went-wrong)).
- One unit's change that cannot be rolled back without rolling back the rest (ours).
- A single-user or internal tool, where a release is a merge and a rollback is a revert (ours).

### Questions to ask of this project

- Which channels exist before stable, and who uses them?
- How are problems reported and watched after a release?
- How is one unit's change rolled back?
- Which paths are read-only and could go first?
- Not released yet: what must exist before the first release?

### Trade-offs

- A canary catches regressions before most users meet them and slows each release (ROL-2).
- A shadow run on real traffic finds divergences tests miss, at the cost of running both paths and
  of the shared services' headroom (ROL-10, OPS-8).

### When not to apply it

- A project not released yet has no channels to measure; the finding is what must exist before the
  first release (ours).
- A tool only its author runs gains little from staged rollout; a quick revert is its rollback
  (ours).

## Q12 guide: How will you measure cost and result?

For question 12 of the [checklist](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/checklist.md): read it before writing up a finding on that
question. It walks through what the cases show; the project's owner decides. Each point names its
evidence: a lesson ID (its strength, its cases and the cases against it are in
[lessons/evidence.md](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/lessons/evidence.md); its page links the case sections) or a case link.
"(ours)" marks the maintainer's reading, evidence level `ours`; so does a lesson tagged `[ours]` there,
which is our inference from its cases.

### Lessons behind it

- [CST-1](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/lessons/cost.md): long runs stayed affordable only with high prompt-cache reuse.
- [CST-2](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/lessons/cost.md), [CST-6](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/lessons/cost.md), [CST-7](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/lessons/cost.md): the full
  bill, the work after merge, and review agents as a multiple of generation.
- [MSR-1](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/lessons/measurement.md), [MSR-2](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/lessons/measurement.md): savings against a
  manual effort that never ran are self-estimates; every rate needs its base.
- [MSR-4](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/lessons/measurement.md), [MSR-5](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/lessons/measurement.md): gains separated from
  other work in the same window; known regressions published as a floor.
- [MSR-9](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/lessons/measurement.md), [MSR-10](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/lessons/measurement.md): people's share measured
  from day one; owners who rejected a change and migrated anyway counted.
- [TST-9](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/lessons/testing.md): performance treated as part of the contract.
- [KNW-3](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/lessons/knowledge.md): structured session logs from the start.

Cases, in our words: GitHub benchmarked before and after (amid other changes) and gave its token
bill; Bun and ts-rust priced tokens at list rates (ts-rust's restart used flat-rate plans); Bun
counted regressions after merge; Google measured shares as edit distance. Every effort or saving
figure is the team's own estimate. Bloomberg also counted undecided pull requests, and owners'
migrations that reused rejected ones. Recording reverts is ours.

### What it looks like in a project

- A manual estimate with no record of how it was made, so no saving can be measured against it
  (MSR-1).
- No baseline of the number the product exists for (speed, latency, memory, quality) on fixed
  hardware before the port ([GitHub](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2026-09-16-github-copilot-runtime-rust.md#numbers), TST-9).
- Token spend known only from the bill, not per run or per unit (CST-1, KNW-3).

### Questions to ask of this project

- What is the manual estimate, and how was it made?
- What number does the product exist for, and is it measured on fixed hardware today?
- Where will tokens or spend, people's hours, pull requests, regressions after merge and reverts be
  recorded?
- Which figures will be measured, and which estimated?

### Trade-offs

- Logging tokens and hours from the start costs a little setup; in one case such logs later
  answered where the time went, and a bill rebuilt afterwards rests on estimates (KNW-3, MSR-9).
- A benchmark amid other changes credits the move with gains it did not make; separating them costs
  extra runs (MSR-4).

### When not to apply it

- A small personal move needs no cost study; the result number and the regressions still tell
  whether it was worth it (ours).
- Published costs from other cases rarely transfer: different models, prices and units (CST-4,
  CST-5).

## Report and record formats

The two routes report and record alike. A migration review follows the
[checklist](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/checklist.md); an AI lessons review follows [applying the lessons](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/docs/applying-lessons.md).
Both write a report, wait for the owner's choice, then keep a record in the measured project. The
report gives findings and options; the owner decides. Each option carries its trade-off, and the
agent's own reading, when it gives one, is labelled as such.

### Migration review report

```markdown
# Before-you-migrate review: <repository>, <YYYY-MM-DD>

Path: first review — <no docs/migration-review.md in the repository>.
Migration: <from> to <to>. Scope measured: <lines and files by kind, units, change rate>.
Bearing on going ahead: <the findings that bear on it, and the decision the owner faces, as the agent's reading>. The decision is the owner's.

## Weigh first
- Q<n>: <a finding the rest depend on (a project rule against the move, no oracle, no baseline), and who decides>.

## Not run
- Q<n>: `<exact command>` — <why it was not run>.

## Ask the owner
- Q<n>: <question>. Default: <assumed if unanswered>.

## Nothing missing
- Q<n> <question>: <measurement>.

## Not applicable yet
- Q<n> <question>: <why, and what must exist first>.

## Findings and options

<If the owner may stop at Q1, give the other findings one line each under "Other findings" instead.>

1. Q<n> <question>: <the finding in a line>.
   Today: <what the repository does, with the measurement>.
   Guide: <the lesson IDs and the case sections you read; "(ours)" where the collection marks the maintainer's reading, "agent's reading" on yours>.
   Links: <the guide's URL, each lesson's aspect page and each case section you read>.
   Options (the owner chooses; leaving it as it is may be one):
   - 1A: <change>. Trade-off: <what it costs, risks or gives up>. Cost: S | M | L.
   - 1B: <another change, or "leave as it is">. Trade-off: <...>. Cost: S | M | L.
   When not to apply: <the guide's points that fit this project, or "none fit">.
   Depends on: <finding numbers, or none>.
   Agent's reading: <the option the measurements favour, and why; or "no lean">.
   Check now: <for each option, a command or count that passes once it is applied>.
   Event that proves it: <what later work must show>.
   Owner's choice: <left blank for the owner: do 1A | do 1B | later | skip>.
2. ...

## Next step
Reply "Apply what you recommended", "Apply 1A and 3B; 2 later; skip 5" or "Apply none; write the record". I then follow checklist "How to run" step 9: the record first, with each chosen proposal's baseline; one proposal at a time, on a branch; I stop at the first failing check, apply nothing after it, and report.
```

Cost: S under a day of agent work, M a few days, L a week or more.

### AI lessons review report

```markdown
# AI lessons review: <project>, <YYYY-MM-DD>

Path: first review — <no docs/ai-lessons-review.md in the project>.
Work measured: <what agents do here: sessions, tasks, reviews, tests, releases>.

## Limits of this run
- Session: fresh | not fresh (<why; a session that ran the work is partly judging itself>).
- Figures: measured from the repository now, or recorded (taken from notes or logs, not re-measured); mark each "recorded" figure below.
- Models: <the models this project uses>; any newer than every case, or with no row in "By model", makes its model-dependent lessons things to re-check, not evidence.

## Not run
- <lesson ID>: `<exact command>` — <why it was not run>.

## Ask the owner
- <lesson ID>: <question>. Default if unanswered: <what you will assume>.

## Findings and options

1. <lesson ID> <the lesson in a few words>: <the finding in a line>.
   Today: <what the project does, with the measurement>.
   Evidence: <the lesson's strength and its "Against" line>; "agent's reading" on your own.
   Links: <the lesson's aspect page and each case section you read>.
   Options (the owner chooses; leaving it as it is may be one):
   - 1A: <change>. Trade-off: <what it costs, risks or gives up>. Cost: S | M | L.
   - 1B: <another change, or "leave as it is">. Trade-off: <...>. Cost: S | M | L.
   Depends on: <finding numbers, or none>.
   Agent's reading: <the option the measurements favour, and why; or "no lean">.
   Check now: <for each option, a command or count that passes once it is applied>.
   Event that proves it: <what later work must show for the change to have held>.
   Owner's choice: <left blank for the owner: do 1A | do 1B | later | skip>.
2. ...

## Next step
Reply "Apply what you recommended", "Apply 1A and 3B; 2 later; skip 5" or "Apply none; write the record". I then follow docs/applying-lessons.md step 6: the record first, with each chosen proposal's baseline; one proposal at a time, on a branch; I stop at the first failing check, apply nothing after it, and report.
```

### Revisit report

Both routes, when the record exists (checklist step 10, [applying the lessons](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/docs/applying-lessons.md)
step 7). Each finding takes the first review's finding format, numbered after the record's last row.

```markdown
# <Before-you-migrate | AI lessons> revisit: <project>, <YYYY-MM-DD>

Path: revisit — <the record found>, which names log entry <date and title>.
Corrections: <each entry: applies or not, what was found, the options; or "corrections.md has no entry">.
Newest log entry: <date and title>. Stop: <yes: same entry and nothing due | no: why>.

## Due first
- #<row> <ID>: waiting for first use, check by <YYYY-MM-DD> passed; owner <who>.

## Re-check
- #<row> <ID>: proven | still waiting | stopped holding | not shown — <the "Check now" output and the numbers against the baseline>.

## Still closed
- #<row> <ID>: skipped | owner's choice, <YYYY-MM-DD> — no new or changed lesson bears on it, and its measurement has not changed.

## Lint
- #<row> <ID>: <the newer lesson that contradicts or supersedes it, or the change to its lesson>.

## Findings and options
<Only new or changed lessons and questions, earlier "later" items, items that stopped holding, what the lint found, and closed items reopened (say why: which new lesson, or which measurement changed).>
## Next step
Reply "Apply what you recommended", "Apply 1A and 3B; 2 later; skip 5" or "Apply none; write the record". I then follow checklist "How to run" step 9 or docs/applying-lessons.md step 6: the record first, with each chosen proposal's baseline; one proposal at a time, on a branch; I stop at the first failing check, apply nothing after it, and report.
```

### The record

A migration review writes `docs/migration-review.md` in the measured repository; an AI lessons
review writes `docs/ai-lessons-review.md` in the project. Same shape; the first lines and the second
column differ:

```markdown
# Migration review record: <repository>

Checklist: <ai-migrations commit or date>. Migration: <from> to <to>.
Log entry: <date and title of the newest log.md entry this review covered>.
Corrections checked: <COR IDs with what was found, or "none listed">, <YYYY-MM-DD>.

| # | Question | Proposal | Baseline | Status | Owner | Check by | Event that shows it | Date |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | Q<n> | <the option the owner chose, in one line> | <how often, evidence> | <status> | <who looks for the event> | <YYYY-MM-DD> | <commit, test run or number> | <YYYY-MM-DD> |
```

```markdown
# AI lessons review record: <project>

Lessons: <ai-migrations commit or date>.
Log entry: <date and title of the newest log.md entry this review covered>.
Corrections checked: <COR IDs with what was found, or "none listed">, <YYYY-MM-DD>.

| # | Lesson | Proposal | Baseline | Status | Owner | Check by | Event that shows it | Date |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | <ID> | <the option the owner chose, in one line> | <how often, evidence> | <status> | <who looks for the event> | <YYYY-MM-DD> | <commit, test run, count or incident> | <YYYY-MM-DD> |
| 3a | <ID> | <one part of a bundled proposal> | ... | ... | ... | ... | ... | ... |
```

Proposal: the option the owner chose ("1A"), with what it changes; a finding put off or declined
keeps its finding in that cell. One status per row: a proposal with parts gets a row per part (3a,
3b...), each with its own status and event. Assumed owner answers go under the table, one line each:
"Assumed: <question> — <default>, <date>". An owner's choice that differs from a lesson or a
question's guide goes there too, one line each: "Owner's choice: #<row> <ID> — <what was chosen>;
reason: <why>; words: "<the owner's words>"; <date>". A revisit proposes a skipped row or an owner's
choice again only for a new or changed lesson or a changed measurement, and says which.

Corrections checked: the [corrections.md](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/corrections.md) entries the last review or revisit
compared with this project, with what it found and the date; a first review writes "none listed"
when the file has no entry.

Baseline: written before any change, how often the proposal's problem happened so far, with the
evidence (a count from the history, logs or incidents), marked "(recorded)" when it comes from notes
rather than a fresh count; a revisit compares the work since with it.

Status, one of: open, proven, waiting for first use, stopped holding, skipped. A proposal the owner
marked "later" is open; one the owner declined is skipped; an applied change whose check failed stays
open, and its event names the failed check. A "do" that waits on an owner action, or on work outside
this session, stays open, and its event says what it waits on. An applied change whose "Check now"
passes is waiting for first use; once later work shows its "Event that proves it", it is proven.

Owner and Check by: every row waiting for first use names who looks for its event and the date by
which the event should have shown if the change holds (when the work that would show it is
expected; the owner of the project sets or changes it). Other rows may leave both "—". A revisit
lists first the rows waiting for first use whose Check by date has passed, with their owner, then
the rest. A record written before these columns existed gets them at its next revisit, and a
record without a "Corrections checked:" line gets one.

## Pitfalls by kind of move

Behaviour the old stack gives without being asked, which a port or restructuring can lose while
the code still compiles. Question 7 of the [checklist](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/checklist.md) uses these lists: search the
scope for each item that applies, give the search you used, and mark the item "like for like" or
"needs a decision". An item with a case link is reported by that case; an item marked (ours) is
our inference. A count only says where to look.

### A JavaScript runtime to a compiled language (for example TypeScript to Rust, Go or C#)

TypeScript's types are erased at run time: the regressions come from what the JavaScript runtime
does underneath them.

- One number type for integers and floats; falsy defaults; time zone; environment reads;
  platform behaviour the old runtime supplied silently, such as a Windows window flag. [GitHub](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2026-09-16-github-copilot-runtime-rust.md)
- Paired operations (open and close, subscribe and unsubscribe) ported on one side only;
  lifecycle and ordering. [GitHub](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2026-09-16-github-copilot-runtime-rust.md)
- Objects that point at each other, which ownership rules turn into copies, indices or callbacks;
  loosely typed return values that need new types; optional arguments that must all be spelled
  out. [Pokémon](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2026-01-25-vjeux-pokemon-showdown-rust.md)
- (ours) Locale; typed arrays and float width; exceptions against error values; shared mutable
  references against ownership; callbacks and closures held across frames; an event loop against
  threads; `undefined`, `null` and absent fields in parsed JSON; DOM or `window` access.

### Python to a compiled language (ours; no case covers it)

- Integers without a size limit; the global interpreter lock hiding data races; `asyncio`'s event
  loop against threads; C extensions and who owns their memory; data saved with `pickle` or other
  Python-only formats; attributes added or patched at run time; truthiness of empty values;
  decorators and metaclasses that generate code.

### Garbage-collected static languages to Rust (Go, Java, C#; ours)

- Ownership of shared mutable state; the choice of async runtime; cancellation (Go's `context`);
  goroutines or threads; map iteration order; the exact bytes a serialiser writes;
  reflection-based decoding (struct tags, annotations); template engines and their escaping; files
  embedded at build time.
- Integer overflow (Go and Java wrap silently; Rust panics in debug builds and wraps in release);
  UTF-16 strings and their indexing (Java, C#) against UTF-8; exceptions against `Result`, and
  which errors the old code let pass.

### C, C++ or Zig to Rust

- Lines that read the same in both languages but behave differently: a side effect inside an
  assertion compiled only in debug builds disappears from release builds; a slice cast panics on
  an odd byte count; colour markers rewritten inside formatted output. [Bun](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2026-07-08-bun-zig-to-rust.md)
- A placeholder constant lowered a limit that real projects reached. [Bun](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2026-07-08-bun-zig-to-rust.md) (ours) Search the
  port for placeholder values left for a later phase.
- A comparison of two pointers by address where the original compared what they point to: safe,
  compiles, and is always false. [Intel](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2026-08-24-intel-ideas-c-to-rust.md)
- Firmware and code that calls hardware or assembly cannot be safe Rust; platforms without the
  Rust compiler or its standard library need extra work. [Intel](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2026-08-24-intel-ideas-c-to-rust.md)
- A faithful port keeps the old design, so some `unsafe` code remains; decide how much the target
  may use and where. [Bun](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2026-07-08-bun-zig-to-rust.md)
- (ours) Integer overflow and wrap; out-of-range float-to-integer casts; aliasing and casts away
  from const; mutable globals; custom allocators; unchecked indexing.

### Widening a type or a data format (for example 32-bit to 64-bit IDs)

- Bit operations that assume the old width; values held in SQL strings and other text the type
  system does not see; test fixtures whose sample values should exceed the old range; golden
  outputs that must be regenerated with the project's own tools. [Google](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2025-04-13-google-int64-ids.md)
- Uses reached only through other variables, several steps from the changed field; an index
  search with a distance limit can miss them. [Google](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2025-04-13-google-int64-ids.md)
- (ours) 64-bit values read as JSON by JavaScript or any reader that keeps numbers as doubles lose
  precision above 2^53; send them as strings.

### Restructuring within one language (monolith to services, an API pattern across call sites)

- The order of schema change, writers and backfill: filling a new column before the code that
  inserts rows is changed can lose rows silently. [1Password](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2026-04-20-1password-monolith-refactor.md)
- Tables or other state shared with other parts of the system, which a new service must not
  treat as its own. [1Password](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2026-04-20-1password-monolith-refactor.md)
- Formats an agent assumes without checking (an identifier's format, for example) and then builds
  on across many changes. [1Password](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2026-04-20-1password-monolith-refactor.md)
- (ours) Deploy order between the old system and the new service, and which side owns each write
  during the switch.

### One test framework to another

- The right replacement often depends on runtime facts (the rendered output a test queries), which
  a syntax-tree rule over one file cannot see; per-method rules for the old library keep growing.
  [Slack](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2024-05-22-slack-enzyme-to-rtl.md)
- Converted files that fail at setup or import hide every test case in them, right or wrong.
  [Slack](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2024-05-22-slack-enzyme-to-rtl.md) (ours) Compare the count of discovered tests before and after the move.
- In-house test runners, rules and shared base classes that no stock rule handles; Uber first
  changed the build so both versions ran side by side, and skipped any file using a pattern its
  recipes did not support. [Uber](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2026-04-07-uber-junit4-to-junit5.md)

### A UI component library or design system to another

- Sizes, spacing scales and grid columns that differ in meaning as well as name: a model mapped
  a medium button to medium where the old medium looked like the new large, and the two grids had
  12 and 24 columns. A page that compiles can render broken: check each page visually. [Zalando](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2025-02-20-zalando-ui-component-libraries.md)
- Properties the target component lacks, which a model may fill with a plausible one that does not
  exist; data passed into a component in a changed shape, which once passed review and broke a
  page in production. [Zalando](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2025-02-20-zalando-ui-component-libraries.md)
- Defaults the old components applied unasked, such as a notification timeout: decide whether to
  keep them. [Zalando](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2025-02-20-zalando-ui-component-libraries.md)

### A cross-platform mobile app to native apps (for example React Native to native iOS and Android code)

- What users and other systems see across the switch: staying signed in, push notifications, and
  analytics events with the context downstream systems read. [Shopify](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2026-09-10-shopify-react-native-to-native.md)
- How long an agent takes to test one change on the target platform: driving simulators through
  screenshots or the accessibility tree took minutes per test, where the edit took seconds; plan a
  headless or command-line path into the app's logic. [Shopify](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2026-09-10-shopify-react-native-to-native.md)
- (ours) Navigation and back stack, deep links, accessibility labels, layout across screen sizes
  and over-the-air updates the cross-platform framework handled.

### A build system or packaging model to another

- Imports that look required in the code but are test-only or conditional; Bloomberg crossed
  syntax-tree imports with modules seen at run time to tell them apart. [Bloomberg](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2026-11-03-bloomberg-python-cpp-uplift.md)
- A wrong dependency choice that builds and passes smoke checks, then fails only once deployed;
  the pipeline also never ran some targets' unit tests. [Bloomberg](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2026-11-03-bloomberg-python-cpp-uplift.md)

### A library or framework upgrade, or a move to its newer API

- Built-ins that replace an old check but accept different input (Angular's email pattern for
  the project's own; plain required for must-be-true on a checkbox); code that changes validators or errors
  imperatively, which the new API rejects; side effects inside checks that now run at another
  time. [Spartacus](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2026-04-13-lutz-leonhardt-spartacus-signal-forms.md)
- (ours) Removed or deprecated APIs; changed defaults; behaviour changes listed only in the release notes
  between the two versions (read them all, not only the latest); transitive dependencies that
  now conflict; generated code or configuration that must be regenerated.
- Equality and hashing that a language upgrade changes under the same source: after Groovy 3 to 4,
  a role and a user of the same name counted as one item in a set, and the admin lost its role.
  [PagerDuty](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2026-04-13-pagerduty-rundeck-grails-7.md)

### A data store to another (for example key-value to relational, or to an analytics store)

- The old store's access pattern: reading key by key on the new engine turns one operation into
  thousands of round trips in a row; Datadog ruled that out and redesigned the schema first.
  [Datadog](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2026-06-23-datadog-foundationdb-to-postgres.md)
- Sums over large values: a ported query that adds a 64-bit column without widening passes on
  small test data and overflows only at production volumes; floating-point sums need a tolerance
  when old and new are compared. [Temporal](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2026-09-02-temporal-billing-store-clickhouse.md)

### Seams

How one unit can switch while the rest stays, used by question 5 of the checklist (ours, except
where a case is linked):

- One framework to another: each file or component moves on its own.
- TypeScript to Rust: a native addon, WebAssembly inside the old app, or a separate process; GitHub
  used a temporary native-addon layer and removed the old code in the same change; a synchronous
  call across that layer froze the app's interface until made asynchronous. [GitHub](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2026-09-16-github-copilot-runtime-rust.md)
- C or C++ to Rust: a C ABI; Intel generated each wrapper's signature with a binding tool and,
  where tests existed (none for libgit2), tested a mixed build after each symbol. [Intel](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2026-08-24-intel-ideas-c-to-rust.md)
- Go, Java or C# to Rust: a process boundary or a C ABI.
- Across a C ABI: who allocates and frees each value, and panics or exceptions that must not
  cross the boundary.
- A service split: route requests per path or tenant to the old or the new side and move the
  routes one at a time (the strangler-fig pattern).
- A cross-platform app to native apps: a fresh native app beside the old one, each screen ported
  against the running old app; Shopify chose this over a gradual move inside the old app. [Shopify](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2026-09-10-shopify-react-native-to-native.md)
- A schema or storage change: expand and contract. Add the new form, write both, backfill, switch
  the reads, then drop the old form; this order avoids the backfill loss 1Password hit.
  [1Password](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2026-04-20-1password-monolith-refactor.md)

### Any move

- Replacement libraries that behave differently from the old ones; one caused an endless loop at
  startup. [GitHub](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2026-09-16-github-copilot-runtime-rust.md) (ours) List each direct dependency, its target library, version, and
  whether that is a stable release or archived.
- Docs and agent instruction files that still recommend the old library steer agents back to it;
  awkward patterns in example code get copied too. [Asana](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2026-08-07-asana-enzyme-to-rtl.md)
- (ours) Source shared with another language or toolchain (shader headers, generated code), which a
  port splits into copies that drift.
- (ours) Bit-exact results across languages (float model, thread count) when tests compare outputs.
- Not a language difference but an agent failure that looks like one: functions left as stubs, or
  missing, behind a clean build; compiler feedback alone lets them through. [Intel](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2026-08-24-intel-ideas-c-to-rust.md), [Bun](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2026-07-08-bun-zig-to-rust.md)
